section.heading: BLACKSTONE RIVER VALLEY NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK.

subsection.heading: Purpose.—
subsection.chapeau: The purpose of this section is to establish the Blackstone River Valley National Historical Park—

paragraph.content: to help preserve, protect, and interpret the nationally significant resources that exemplify the industrial heritage of the Blackstone River Valley for the benefit and inspiration of future generations;

to support the preservation, protection, and interpretation of the urban, rural, and agricultural landscape features (including the Blackstone River and Canal) of the region that provide an overarching context for the industrial heritage of the Blackstone River Valley;

paragraph.chapeau: to educate the public about—

subparagraph.content: the nationally significant sites and districts that convey the industrial history of the Blackstone River Valley; and
the significance of the Blackstone River Valley to the past and present of the United States; and

paragraph.content: to support and enhance the network of partners in the protection, improvement, management, and operation of related resources and facilities throughout the John H. Chafee Blackstone River Valley National Heritage Corridor.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: National heritage corridor.—
paragraph.content: The term “National Heritage Corridor” means the John H. Chafee Blackstone River Valley National Heritage Corridor.

paragraph.heading: Park.—
paragraph.content: The term “Park” means the Blackstone River Valley National Historical Park established by subsection (c)(1).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: States.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “States” means—

subparagraph.content: the State of Massachusetts; and
the State of Rhode Island.

subsection.heading: Blackstone River Valley National Historical Park.—

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: There is established in the States a unit of the National Park System, to be known as the “Blackstone River Valley National Historical Park”.

paragraph.heading: Historic sites and districts.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Park shall include—

subparagraph.content: Blackstone River State Park; and

subparagraph.chapeau: the following resources, as described in Management Option 3 of the study entitled “Blackstone River Valley Special Resource Study—Study Report 2011”:

clause.content: Old Slater Mill National Historic Landmark District.
Slatersville Historic District.
Ashton Historic District.
Whitinsville Historic District.
Hopedale Village Historic District.
Blackstone River and the tributaries of Blackstone River.
Blackstone Canal.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Secretary may acquire land or interests in land that are considered contributing historic resources in the historic sites and districts described in paragraph (2)(B) for inclusion in the Park boundary by donation, purchase from a willing seller with donated or appropriated funds, or exchange.

clause.heading: No condemnation.—
clause.content: No land or interest in land may be acquired for the Park by condemnation.

subparagraph.heading: Park boundary.—
subparagraph.content: On a determination by the Secretary that a sufficient quantity of land or interests in land has been acquired to constitute a manageable park unit, the Secretary shall establish a boundary for the Park by publishing a boundary map in the Federal Register.

subparagraph.heading: Other resources.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may include in the Park boundary any resources that are the subject of an agreement with the States or a subdivision of the States entered into under paragraph (4)(D).

subparagraph.heading: Boundary adjustment.—
subparagraph.content: On the acquisition of additional land or interests in land under subparagraph (A), or on entering an agreement under subparagraph (C), the boundary of the Park shall be adjusted to reflect the acquisition or agreement by publishing a Park boundary map in the Federal Register.

subparagraph.heading: Availability of map.—
subparagraph.content: The maps referred to in this paragraph shall be available for public inspection in the appropriate offices of the National Park Service.

subparagraph.heading: Administrative facilities.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may acquire not more than 10 acres in Woonsocket, Rhode Island for the development of administrative, curatorial, maintenance, or visitor facilities for the Park.

subparagraph.heading: Limitation.—
subparagraph.content: Land owned by the States or a political subdivision of the States may be acquired under this paragraph only by donation.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer land within the boundary of the Park in accordance with—

clause.content: this subsection; and

clause.chapeau: the laws generally applicable to units of the National Park System, including—

subclause.content: the National Park Service Organic Act (16 U.S.C. 1 et seq.); and
the Act of August 21, 1935 (16 U.S.C. 461 et seq.).

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: Not later than 3 years after the date on which funds are made available to carry out this subsection, the Secretary shall prepare a general management plan for the Park—

subclause.content: in consultation with the States and other interested parties; and
in accordance with section 12(b) of the National Park System General Authorities Act (16 U.S.C. 1a-7(b)).

clause.heading: Requirements.—
clause.chapeau: The plan shall consider ways to use preexisting or planned visitor facilities and recreational opportunities developed in the National Heritage Corridor, including—

subclause.content: the Blackstone Valley Visitor Center, Pawtucket, Rhode Island;
the Captain Wilbur Kelly House, Blackstone River State Park, Lincoln, Rhode Island;
the Museum of Work and Culture, Woonsocket, Rhode Island;
the River Bend Farm/Blackstone River and Canal Heritage State Park, Uxbridge, Massachusetts;
the Worcester Blackstone Visitor Center, located at the former Washburn & Moen wire mill facility, Worcester, Massachusetts;
the Route 295 Visitor Center adjacent to Blackstone River State Park; and
the Blackstone River Bikeway.

subparagraph.heading: Related sites.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may provide technical assistance, visitor services, interpretive tours, and educational programs to sites and resources in the National Heritage Corridor that are located outside the boundary of the Park and associated with the purposes for which the Park is established.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: To further the purposes of this subsection and notwithstanding chapter 63 of title 31, United States Code, the Secretary may enter into cooperative agreements with the States, political subdivisions of the States, nonprofit organizations (including the local coordinating entity for the National Heritage Corridor), and other interested parties—

subclause.content: to provide technical assistance, interpretation, and educational programs in the historic sites and districts described in paragraph (2)(B); and

subject to the availability of appropriations and clauses (ii) and (iii), to provide not more than 50 percent of the cost of any natural, historic, or cultural resource protection project in the Park that is consistent with the general management plan prepared under subparagraph (B).

clause.heading: Matching requirement.—
clause.content: As a condition of the receipt of funds under clause (i)(II), the Secretary shall require that any Federal funds made available under a cooperative agreement entered into under this paragraph are to be matched on a 1-to-1 basis by non-Federal funds.

clause.heading: Reimbursement.—
clause.chapeau: Any payment made by the Secretary under clause (i)(ii) shall be subject to an agreement that the conversion, use, or disposal of the project for purposes that are inconsistent with the purposes of this subsection, as determined by the Secretary, shall result in a right of the United States to reimbursement of the greater of—

subclause.content: the amount provided by the Secretary to the project under clause (i)(II); or
an amount equal to the increase in the value of the project that is attributable to the funds, as determined by the Secretary at the time of the conversion, use, or disposal.

clause.heading: Public access.—
clause.content: Any cooperative agreement entered into under this subparagraph shall provide for reasonable public access to the resources covered by the cooperative agreement.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Congress dedicates the Park to John H. Chafee, the former United States Senator from Rhode Island, in recognition of—

clause.content: the role of John H. Chafee in the preservation of the resources of the Blackstone River Valley and the heritage corridor that bears the name of John H. Chafee; and
the decades of the service of John H. Chafee to the people of Rhode Island and the United States.

subparagraph.heading: Memorial.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall display a memorial at an appropriate location in the Park that recognizes the role of John H. Chafee in preserving the resources of the Blackstone River Valley for the people of the United States.

section.heading: COLTSVILLE NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: City.—
paragraph.content: The term “city” means the city of Hartford, Connecticut.

paragraph.heading: Commission.—
paragraph.content: The term “Commission” means the Coltsville National Historical Park Advisory Commission established by subsection (k)(1).

paragraph.heading: Historic district.—
paragraph.content: The term “Historic District” means the Coltsville Historic District.

paragraph.heading: Map.—
paragraph.content: The term “map” means the map entitled “Coltsville National Historical Park—Proposed Boundary”, numbered T25/102087, and dated May 11, 2010.

paragraph.heading: Park.—
paragraph.content: The term “park” means the Coltsville National Historical Park in the State of Connecticut.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of Connecticut.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), there is established in the State a unit of the National Park System to be known as the “Coltsville National Historical Park”.

paragraph.heading: Conditions for establishment.—
paragraph.chapeau: The park shall not be established until the date on which the Secretary determines that—

subparagraph.content: the Secretary has acquired by donation sufficient land or an interest in land within the boundary of the park to constitute a manageable unit;

the State, city, or private property owner, as appropriate, has entered into a written agreement with the Secretary to donate at least 10,000 square feet of space in the Colt Armory Complex which would include facilities for park administration and visitor services; and

the Secretary has entered into a written agreement with the State, city, or other public entity, as appropriate, providing that land owned by the State, city, or other public entity within the Coltsville Historic District shall be managed consistent with this section.

paragraph.heading: Notice.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 30 days after the date on which the Secretary makes a determination under paragraph (2), the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register notice of the establishment of the park.

subsection.heading: Boundaries.—
subsection.chapeau: The park shall include and provide appropriate interpretation and viewing of the following sites, as generally depicted on the map:

paragraph.content: The East Armory.
The Church of the Good Shepherd.
The Caldwell/Colt Memorial Parish House.
Colt Park.
The Potsdam Cottages.
Armsmear.
The James Colt House.

subsection.heading: Availability of Map.—
subsection.content: The map shall be on file and available for public inspection in appropriate offices of the National Park Service.

subsection.heading: Collections.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may enter into a written agreement with the State of Connecticut State Library, Wadsworth Atheneum, and the Colt Trust, or other public entities, as appropriate, to gain appropriate access to Colt-related artifacts for the purposes of having items routinely on display in the East Armory or within other areas of the park to enhance the visitor experience.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer the park in accordance with—

subparagraph.content: this section; and

subparagraph.chapeau: the laws generally applicable to units of the National Park System, including—

clause.content: the National Park Service Organic Act (16 U.S.C. 1 et seq.); and
the Act of August 21, 1935 (16 U.S.C. 461 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: State and local jurisdiction.—
paragraph.chapeau: Nothing in this section enlarges, diminishes, or modifies any authority of the State, or any political subdivision of the State (including the city)—

subparagraph.content: to exercise civil and criminal jurisdiction; or
to carry out State laws (including regulations) and rules on non-Federal land located within the boundary of the park.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: As the Secretary determines to be appropriate to carry out this section, the Secretary may enter into cooperative agreements to carry out this section, under which the Secretary may identify, interpret, restore, rehabilitate, and provide technical assistance for the preservation of nationally significant properties within the boundary of the park.

paragraph.heading: Right of access.—
paragraph.chapeau: A cooperative agreement entered into under paragraph (1) shall provide that the Secretary, acting through the Director of the National Park Service, shall have the right of access at all reasonable times to all public portions of the property covered by the agreement for the purposes of—

subparagraph.content: conducting visitors through the properties; and
interpreting the properties for the public.

paragraph.heading: Changes or alterations.—
paragraph.content: No changes or alterations shall be made to any properties covered by a cooperative agreement entered into under paragraph (1) unless the Secretary and the other party to the agreement agree to the changes or alterations.

paragraph.heading: Conversion, use, or disposal.—
paragraph.chapeau: Any payment by the Secretary under this subsection shall be subject to an agreement that the conversion, use, or disposal of a project for purposes contrary to the purposes of this section, as determined by the Secretary, shall entitle the United States to reimbursement in an amount equal to the greater of—

subparagraph.content: the amounts made available to the project by the United States; or
the portion of the increased value of the project attributable to the amounts made available under this subsection, as determined at the time of the conversion, use, or disposal.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: As a condition of the receipt of funds under this subsection, the Secretary shall require that any Federal funds made available under a cooperative agreement shall be matched on a 1-to-1 basis by non-Federal funds.

subparagraph.heading: Form.—
subparagraph.content: With the approval of the Secretary, the non-Federal share required under subparagraph (A) may be in the form of donated property, goods, or services from a non-Federal source, fairly valued.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary is authorized to acquire land and interests in land by donation, purchase with donated or appropriated funds, or exchange, except that land or interests in land owned by the State or any political subdivision of the State may be acquired only by donation.

paragraph.heading: No condemnation.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may not acquire any land or interest in land for the purposes of this section by condemnation.

subsection.heading: Technical Assistance and Public Interpretation.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide technical assistance and public interpretation of related historic and cultural resources within the boundary of the historic district.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 3 fiscal years after the date on which funds are made available to carry out this section, the Secretary, in consultation with the Commission, shall complete a management plan for the park in accordance with—

subparagraph.content: section 12(b) of Public Law 91-383 (commonly known as the “National Park Service General Authorities Act”) (16 U.S.C. 1a-7(b)); and
other applicable laws.

paragraph.heading: Cost share.—
paragraph.content: The management plan shall include provisions that identify costs to be shared by the Federal Government, the State, and the city, and other public or private entities or individuals for necessary capital improvements to, and maintenance and operations of, the park.

paragraph.heading: Submission to congress.—
paragraph.chapeau: On completion of the management plan, the Secretary shall submit the management plan to—

subparagraph.content: the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives; and
the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate.

subsection.heading: Coltsville National Historical Park Advisory Commission.—

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: There is established a Commission to be known as the “Coltsville National Historical Park Advisory Commission”.

paragraph.heading: Duty.—
paragraph.content: The Commission shall advise the Secretary in the development and implementation of the management plan.

subparagraph.heading: Composition.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Commission shall be composed of 11 members, to be appointed by the Secretary, of whom—

clause.content: 2 members shall be appointed after consideration of recommendations submitted by the Governor of the State;
1 member shall be appointed after consideration of recommendations submitted by the State Senate President;
1 member shall be appointed after consideration of recommendations submitted by the Speaker of the State House of Representatives;
2 members shall be appointed after consideration of recommendations submitted by the Mayor of Hartford, Connecticut;
2 members shall be appointed after consideration of recommendations submitted by Connecticut’s 2 United States Senators;
1 member shall be appointed after consideration of recommendations submitted by Connecticut’s First Congressional District Representative;
2 members shall have experience with national parks and historic preservation;
all appointments must have significant experience with and knowledge of the Coltsville Historic District; and
1 member of the Commission must live in the Sheldon/Charter Oak neighborhood within the Coltsville Historic District.

subparagraph.heading: Initial appointments.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall appoint the initial members of the Commission not later than the earlier of—

clause.content: the date that is 30 days after the date on which the Secretary has received all of the recommendations for appointments under subparagraph (A); or
the date that is 30 days after the park is established.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: A member shall be appointed for a term of 3 years.

clause.heading: Reappointment.—
clause.content: A member may be reappointed for not more than 1 additional term.

subparagraph.heading: Vacancies.—
subparagraph.content: A vacancy on the Commission shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment was made.

paragraph.heading: Meetings.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Commission shall meet at the call of—

subparagraph.content: the Chairperson; or
a majority of the members of the Commission.

paragraph.heading: Quorum.—
paragraph.content: A majority of the Commission shall constitute a quorum.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Commission shall select a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson from among the members of the Commission.

subparagraph.heading: Vice chairperson.—
subparagraph.content: The Vice Chairperson shall serve as Chairperson in the absence of the Chairperson.

subparagraph.heading: Term.—
subparagraph.content: A member may serve as Chairperson or Vice Chairperson for not more than 1 year in each office.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Members of the Commission shall serve without compensation.

clause.heading: Travel expenses.—
clause.content: Members of the Commission shall be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, at rates authorized for an employee of an agency under subchapter I of chapter 57 of title 5, United States Code, while away from the home or regular place of business of the member in the performance of the duty of the Commission.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Secretary shall provide the Commission with any staff members and technical assistance that the Secretary, after consultation with the Commission, determines to be appropriate to enable the Commission to carry out the duty of the Commission.

clause.heading: Detail of employees.—
clause.content: The Secretary may accept the services of personnel detailed from the State or any political subdivision of the State.

paragraph.heading: Nonapplicability of chapter 10 of title 5, united states code.—
paragraph.content: Section 1013(b) of title 5, United States Code, shall not apply to the Commission.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Unless extended under subparagraph (B), the Commission shall terminate on the date that is 10 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

clause.heading: Recommendation.—
clause.content: Eight years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Commission shall make a recommendation to the Secretary if a body of its nature is still necessary to advise on the development of the park.

clause.heading: Term of extension.—
clause.content: If, based on a recommendation under clause (i), the Secretary determines that the Commission is still necessary, the Secretary may extend the life of the Commission for not more than 10 years.

section.heading: FIRST STATE NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Historical park.—
paragraph.content: The term “historical park” means the First State National Historical Park.

paragraph.heading: Map.—
paragraph.content: The term “map” means the map with pages numbered 1-6 entitled “First State National Historical Park, New Castle, Kent, Sussex Counties, DE and Delaware County, PA, Proposed Boundary”, numbered T19/80,000G, and dated October 2014.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: Redesignation of first state national monument.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The First State National Monument is redesignated as the First State National Historical Park, as generally depicted on the map.

subparagraph.heading: Availability of funds.—
subparagraph.content: Any funds available for purposes of the First State National Monument shall be available for purposes of the historical park.

subparagraph.heading: References.—
subparagraph.content: Any references in a law, regulation, document, record, map, or other paper of the United States to the First State National Monument shall be considered to be a reference to the historical park.

paragraph.heading: Purposes.—
paragraph.chapeau: The purposes of the historical park are to preserve, protect, and interpret the nationally significant cultural and historic resources that are associated with—

subparagraph.content: early Dutch, Swedish, and English settlement of the Colony of Delaware and portions of the Colony of Pennsylvania; and

subparagraph.chapeau: the role of Delaware—

clause.content: in the birth of the United States; and
as the first State to ratify the Constitution.

paragraph.heading: Inclusion of additional historic sites.—
paragraph.chapeau: In addition to sites included in the historical park (as redesignated by paragraph (1)(A)) as of the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary may include the following sites within the boundary of the historical park, as generally depicted on the map:

subparagraph.content: Fort Christina National Historic Landmark in New Castle County, Delaware, as depicted on page 3 of 6 of the map.
Old Swedes Church National Historic Landmark in New Castle County, Delaware, as depicted on page 3 of 6 of the map.
John Dickinson Plantation National Historic Landmark in Kent County, Delaware, as depicted on page 5 of 6 of the map.
Ryves Holt House in Sussex County, Delaware, as depicted on page 6 of 6 of the map.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer the historical park in accordance with—

subparagraph.content: this section; and

subparagraph.chapeau: the laws generally applicable to units of the National Park System, including—

clause.content: the National Park System Organic Act (16 U.S.C. 1 et seq.); and
the Act of August 21, 1935 (16 U.S.C. 461 et seq.).

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Except as provided in clause (ii), the Secretary may acquire all or a portion of any of the sites described in subsection (b)(3), including easements or other interests in land, by purchase from a willing seller, donation, or exchange.

clause.heading: Donation only.—
clause.content: The Secretary may acquire only by donation all or a portion of the property identified as “Area for Potential Addition by Donation” on page 2 of 6 of the map.

clause.heading: Limitation.—
clause.content: No land or interest land may be acquired for inclusion in the historical park by condemnation.

subparagraph.heading: Boundary adjustment.—
subparagraph.content: On acquisition of land or an interest in land under subparagraph (A), the boundary of the historical park shall be adjusted to reflect the acquisition.

paragraph.heading: Interpretive tours.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary may provide interpretive tours to sites and resources in the State that are located outside the boundary of the historical park and associated with the purposes for which the historical park is established, including—

subparagraph.content: Fort Casimir;
DeVries Monument;
Amstel House;
Dutch House; and
Zwaanendael Museum.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may enter into a cooperative agreement with the State of Delaware, political subdivisions of the State of Delaware, institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, and individuals to mark, interpret, and restore nationally significant historic or cultural resources within the boundaries of the historical park, if the cooperative agreement provides for reasonable public access to the resources.

clause.heading: Federal share.—
clause.content: The Federal share of the total cost of any activity carried out under a cooperative agreement entered into under subparagraph (A) shall be not more than 50 percent.

clause.heading: Form of non-federal share.—
clause.content: The non-Federal share may be in the form of in-kind contributions or goods or services fairly valued.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 3 fiscal years after the date on which funds are made available to carry out this paragraph, the Secretary shall complete a management plan for the historical park.

subparagraph.heading: Applicable law.—
subparagraph.content: The management plan shall be prepared in accordance with section 12(b) of the National Park System General Authorities Act (16 U.S.C. 1a-7(b)) and other applicable laws.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 3 years after the date on which funds are made available to carry out this section, the Secretary shall complete a study assessing the historical significance of additional properties in the State of Delaware that are associated with the purposes of historical park.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.content: The study prepared under paragraph (1) shall include an assessment of the potential for designating the additional properties as National Historic Landmarks.

subsection.heading: Offset.—
subsection.content: Section 7302(f) of the Omnibus Public Land Management Act of 2009 (16 U.S.C. 469n(f)) is amended by inserting before the period at the end the following: “, except that the amount authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section not appropriated as of the date of enactment of the First State National Historical Park Act shall be reduced by $6,500,000”.

section.heading: GETTYSBURG NATIONAL MILITARY PARK.

subsection.heading: Boundary Revision.—
subsection.chapeau: Section 1(b) of Public Law 101-377 (16 U.S.C. 430g-4(b)) is amended—

paragraph.content: at the end of paragraph (1) (as designated by paragraph (1)), by striking the period and inserting “; and”; and

by adding at the end the following:
“(2) the properties depicted as ‘Proposed Addition’ on the map entitled ‘Gettysburg National Military Park Proposed Boundary Addition’, numbered 305/80,045, and dated January, 2010 (2 sheets), including—
“(A) the property commonly known as the ‘Gettysburg Train Station’; and
“(B) the property located adjacent to Plum Run in Cumberland Township.”
.

subsection.heading: Acquisition of Land.—
subsection.chapeau: Section 2(a) of Public Law 101-377 (16 U.S.C. 430g-5(a)) is amended—

paragraph.content:
in the second sentence, by striking “In acquiring” and inserting the following:
“(2) Minimum federal interests.—In acquiring” ; and

by adding at the end the following:
“(3) Method of acquisition for certain land.—Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Secretary may acquire the properties added to the park by section 1(b)(2) only by donation.” .

section.heading: HARRIET TUBMAN UNDERGROUND RAILROAD NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK, MARYLAND.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Historical park.—
paragraph.content: The term “historical park” means the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park established by subsection (b)(1)(A).

paragraph.heading: Map.—
paragraph.content: The term “map” means the map entitled “Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park, Proposed Boundary and Authorized Acquisition Areas”, numbered T20/80,001A, and dated March 2014.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of Maryland.

subsection.heading: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: There is established as a unit of the National Park System the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park in the State, consisting of the area depicted on the map as “Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park Boundary”.

subparagraph.heading: Boundary.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The boundary of the historical park shall consist of—

clause.content: the land described in subparagraph (A); and
any land and interests in land acquired under paragraph (3).

subparagraph.heading: Availability of map.—
subparagraph.content: The map shall be on file and available for public inspection in appropriate offices of the National Park Service.

paragraph.heading: Purpose.—
paragraph.content: The purpose of the historical park is to preserve and interpret for the benefit of present and future generations the historical, cultural, and natural resources associated with the life of Harriet Tubman and the Underground Railroad.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may acquire land and interests in land within the areas depicted on the map as “Authorized Acquisition Areas for the National Historical Park” only by purchase from willing sellers, donation, or exchange.

subparagraph.heading: Limitation.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may not acquire land or an interest in land for purposes of this section by condemnation.

subparagraph.heading: Boundary adjustment.—
subparagraph.content: On acquisition of land or an interest in land under subparagraph (A), the boundary of the historical park shall be adjusted to reflect the acquisition.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall administer the historical park and the portion of the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Monument administered by the National Park Service as a single unit of the National Park System, which shall be known as the “Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park”.

paragraph.heading: Applicable law.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer the historical park in accordance with this section, Presidential Proclamation Number 8943 (78 Fed. Reg. 18763), and the laws generally applicable to units of the National Park System, including—

subparagraph.content: the National Park System Organic Act (16 U.S.C. 1 et seq.); and
the Act of August 21, 1935 (16 U.S.C. 461 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Interagency agreement.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Director of the National Park Service and the Director of the United States Fish and Wildlife Service shall enter into an agreement to allow the National Park Service to provide for archeological research and the public interpretation of historic resources located within the boundary of the Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge that are associated with the life of Harriet Tubman, consistent with the management requirements of the Refuge.

paragraph.heading: Interpretive tours.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may provide interpretive tours to sites and resources located outside the boundary of the historical park in Caroline, Dorchester, and Talbot Counties, Maryland, relating to the life of Harriet Tubman and the Underground Railroad.

paragraph.heading: Land uses and agreements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Nothing in this section affects—

subparagraph.content: land within the boundaries of the Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge;
agreements between the Secretary and private landowners regarding hunting, fishing, farming, or other activities; or

land use rights of private property owners within or adjacent to the historical park or the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Monument, including activities or uses on private land that can be seen or heard within the historical park or the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Monument.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary may enter into an agreement with the State, political subdivisions of the State, colleges and universities, non-profit organizations, and individuals—

clause.content: to mark, interpret, and restore nationally significant historic or cultural resources relating to the life of Harriet Tubman or the Underground Railroad within the boundaries of the historical park, if the agreement provides for reasonable public access; or
to conduct research relating to the life of Harriet Tubman and the Underground Railroad.

subparagraph.heading: Visitor center.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary may enter into an agreement to design, construct, operate, and maintain a joint visitor center on land owned by the State—

clause.content: to provide for National Park Service visitor and interpretive facilities for the historical park; and
to provide to the Secretary, at no additional cost, sufficient office space to administer the historical park.

clause.heading: Federal share.—
clause.content: The Federal share of the total cost of any activity carried out under this paragraph shall not exceed 50 percent.

clause.heading: Form of non-federal share.—
clause.content: The non-Federal share of the cost of carrying out an activity under this paragraph may be in the form of in-kind contributions or goods or services fairly valued.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 3 years after the date on which funds are made available to carry out this section, the Secretary shall prepare a general management plan for the historical park in accordance with section 12(b) of the National Park Service General Authorities Act (16 U.S.C. 1a-7(b)).

paragraph.heading: Consultation.—
paragraph.content: The general management plan shall be prepared in consultation with the State (including political subdivisions of the State).

paragraph.heading: Public comment.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: hold not less than 1 public meeting in the area of the historical park on the proposed general management plan, including opportunity for public comment; and
publish the draft general management plan on the internet and provide an opportunity for public comment on the plan.

paragraph.heading: Coordination.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall coordinate the preparation and implementation of the management plan with—

subparagraph.content: the Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge;
the Harriet Tubman National Historical Park established by section 3036; and
the National Underground Railroad Network to Freedom.

section.heading: HARRIET TUBMAN NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK, AUBURN, NEW YORK.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Historical park.—
paragraph.content: The term “historical park” means the Harriet Tubman National Historical Park established by subsection (b)(1)(A).

paragraph.heading: Home.—
paragraph.content: The term “Home” means The Harriet Tubman Home, Inc., located in Auburn, New York.

paragraph.heading: Map.—
paragraph.content: The term “map” means the map entitled “Harriet Tubman National Historical Park”, numbered T18/80,000, and dated March 2009.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of New York.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), there is established the Harriet Tubman National Historical Park in Auburn, New York, as a unit of the National Park System.

subparagraph.heading: Determination by secretary.—
subparagraph.content: The historical park shall not be established until the date on which the Secretary determines that a sufficient quantity of land, or interests in land, has been acquired to constitute a manageable park unit.

subparagraph.heading: Notice.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 30 days after the date on which the Secretary makes a determination under subparagraph (B), the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register notice of the establishment of the historical park.

subparagraph.heading: Map.—
subparagraph.content: The map shall be on file and available for public inspection in appropriate offices of the National Park Service.

paragraph.heading: Boundary.—
paragraph.content: The historical park shall include the Harriet Tubman Home, the Tubman Home for the Aged, the Thompson Memorial AME Zion Church and Rectory, and associated land, as identified in the area entitled “National Historical Park Proposed Boundary” on the map.

paragraph.heading: Purpose.—
paragraph.content: The purpose of the historical park is to preserve and interpret for the benefit of present and future generations the historical, cultural, and natural resources associated with the life of Harriet Tubman.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may acquire land and interests in land within the areas depicted on the map by purchase from a willing seller, donation, or exchange.

subparagraph.heading: No condemnation.—
subparagraph.content: No land or interest in land within the areas depicted on the map may be acquired by condemnation.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer the historical park in accordance with this section and the laws generally applicable to units of the National Park System, including—

subparagraph.content: the National Park System Organic Act (16 U.S.C. 1 et seq.); and
the Act of August 21, 1935 (16 U.S.C. 461 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Interpretive tours.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may provide interpretive tours to sites and resources located outside the boundary of the historical park in Auburn, New York, relating to the life of Harriet Tubman.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary may enter into an agreement with the owner of any land within the historical park to mark, interpret, or restore nationally significant historic or cultural resources relating to the life of Harriet Tubman, if the agreement provides that—

clause.chapeau: the Secretary shall have the right of access to any public portions of the land covered by the agreement to allow for—

subclause.content: access at reasonable times by historical park visitors to the land; and
interpretation of the land for the public; and

clause.content: no changes or alterations shall be made to the land except by mutual agreement of the Secretary and the owner of the land.

subparagraph.heading: Research.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may enter into an agreement with the State, political subdivisions of the State, institutions of higher education, the Home and other nonprofit organizations, and individuals to conduct research relating to the life of Harriet Tubman.

clause.heading: Federal share.—
clause.content: The Federal share of the total cost of any activity carried out under this paragraph shall not exceed 50 percent.

clause.heading: Form of non-federal share.—
clause.content: The non-Federal share may be in the form of in-kind contributions or goods or services fairly valued.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Secretary shall submit to the Attorney General for review any agreement under this paragraph involving religious property or property owned by a religious institution.

clause.heading: Finding.—
clause.content: No agreement subject to review under this subparagraph shall take effect until the date on which the Attorney General issues a finding that the proposed agreement does not violate the Establishment Clause of the first amendment to the Constitution.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 3 years after the date on which funds are made available to carry out this section, the Secretary shall prepare a general management plan for the historical park in accordance with section 12(b) of the National Park Service General Authorities Act (16 U.S.C. 1a-7(b)).

paragraph.heading: Coordination.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall coordinate the preparation and implementation of the management plan with—

subparagraph.content: the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park established by section 303518; and

footnote.p: Section 601(d) of Public Law 114–289 provides for an amendment as follows: “[s]ection 3036(d)(4)(B) of title XXX of the Carl Levin and Howard P. ‘Buck’ McKeon National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2015 (Public Law 113–291; 128 Stat. 3780) is amended by striking ‘section 2(b)(1)’ and inserting ‘section 3035’”. Such amendment was carried out to subsection (d)(2)(A) in order to reflect the probable intent of Congress since there isn’t a paragraph (4) in such subsection (d).

subparagraph.content: the National Underground Railroad Network to Freedom.

subsection.heading: Offset.—
subsection.content: Section 101(b)(12) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (Public Law 104-303; 110 Stat. 3667) is amended by striking “$53,852,000” and inserting “$29,852,000”.

section.heading: HINCHLIFFE STADIUM ADDITION TO PATERSON GREAT FALLS NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK.

subsection.heading: Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park Boundary Adjustment.—
subsection.chapeau: Section 7001 of the Omnibus Public Land Management Act of 2009 (16 U.S.C. 410lll) is amended as follows:

paragraph.chapeau: In subsection (b)(3)—

subparagraph.content: by striking “The Park shall” and inserting “(A) The Park shall”;
by redesignating subparagraphs (A) through (G) as clauses (i) through (vii), respectively; and

by adding at the end the following:
“(B) In addition to the lands described in subparagraph (A), the Park shall include the approximately 6 acres of land containing Hinchliffe Stadium and generally depicted as the ‘Boundary Modification Area’ on the map entitled ‘Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park, Proposed Boundary Modification’, numbered T03/120,155A, and dated August 2015, which shall be administered as part of the Park in accordance with subsection (c)(1) and section 3 of the Hinchliffe Stadium Heritage Act.” .

paragraph.content: In subsection (b)(4), by striking “The Map” and inserting “The Map and the map referred to in paragraph (3)(B)”.

paragraph.chapeau: In subsection (c)(4)—

subparagraph.content: in subparagraph (A), by striking “The Secretary” and inserting “Except as provided in subparagraphs (B) and (C), the Secretary”; and

by inserting after subparagraph (B) the following:
“(C) Hinchliffe stadium.—The Secretary may not acquire fee title to Hinchliffe Stadium, but may acquire a preservation easement in Hinchliffe Stadium if the Secretary determines that doing so will facilitate resource protection of the stadium.” .

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: In administering the approximately 6 acres of land containing Hinchliffe Stadium and generally depicted as the “Boundary Modification Area” on the map entitled “Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park, Proposed Boundary Modification”, numbered T03/120,155, and dated April 2014, the Secretary of the Interior—

subparagraph.content: may not include non-Federal property within the approximately 6 acres of land as part of Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park without the written consent of the owner;
may not acquire by condemnation any land or interests in land within the approximately 6 acres of land; and
shall not construe the inclusion of Hinchliffe Stadium made by this section to create buffer zones outside the boundaries of the Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park.

paragraph.heading: Outside activities.—
paragraph.content: The fact that activities can be seen or head from within the approximately 6 acres of land described in paragraph (1) shall not preclude such activities outside the boundary of the Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park.

section.heading: LOWER EAST SIDE TENEMENT NATIONAL HISTORIC SITE.

paragraph.chapeau: in section 101(a)—

subparagraph.content: in paragraph (4), by striking “the Lower East Side Tenement at 97 Orchard Street in New York City is an outstanding survivor” and inserting “the Lower East Side Tenements at 97 and 103 Orchard Street in New York City are outstanding survivors”; and

section.heading: MANHATTAN PROJECT NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK.

subsection.heading: Purposes.—
subsection.chapeau: The purposes of this section are—

paragraph.content: to preserve and protect for the benefit of present and future generations the nationally significant historic resources associated with the Manhattan Project;
to improve public understanding of the Manhattan Project and the legacy of the Manhattan Project through interpretation of the historic resources associated with the Manhattan Project;
to enhance public access to the Historical Park consistent with protection of public safety, national security, and other aspects of the mission of the Department of Energy; and

to assist the Department of Energy, Historical Park communities, historical societies, and other interested organizations and individuals in efforts to preserve and protect the historically significant resources associated with the Manhattan Project.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Historical park.—
paragraph.content: The term “Historical Park” means the Manhattan Project National Historical Park established under subsection (c).

paragraph.heading: Manhattan project.—
paragraph.content: The term “Manhattan Project” means the Federal military program to develop an atomic bomb ending on December 31, 1946.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Manhattan Project National Historical Park.—

subparagraph.heading: Date.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this section, there shall be established as a unit of the National Park System the Manhattan Project National Historical Park.

subparagraph.heading: Areas included.—
subparagraph.content: The Historical Park shall consist of facilities and areas listed under paragraph (2) as determined by the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Energy. The Secretary shall include the area referred to in paragraph (2)(C)(i), the B Reactor National Historic Landmark, in the Historical Park.

paragraph.heading: Eligible areas.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Historical Park may only be comprised of one or more of the following areas, or portions of the areas, as generally depicted in the map titled “Manhattan Project National Historical Park Sites”, numbered 540/108,834-C, and dated September 2012:

subparagraph.heading: Oak ridge, tennessee.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Facilities, land, or interests in land that are—

clause.content: Buildings 9204-3 and 9731 at the Department of Energy Y-12 National Security Complex;
the X-10 Graphite Reactor at the Department of Energy Oak Ridge National Laboratory;
the K-25 Building site at the Department of Energy East Tennessee Technology Park;
the former Guest House located at 210 East Madison Road; and

at other sites in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, that are not depicted on the map but are determined by the Secretary to be suitable and appropriate for inclusion in the Historical Park, except that sites administered by the Secretary of Energy may be included only with the concurrence of the Secretary of Energy.

subparagraph.heading: Los alamos, new mexico.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Facilities, land, or interests in land that are—

clause.content: within the Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory National Historic Landmark District, or any addition to the Landmark District proposed in the National Historic Landmark Nomination—Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory (LASL) NHL District (Working Draft of NHL Revision), Los Alamos National Laboratory document LA-UR 12-00387 (January 26, 2012);
the former East Cafeteria located at 1670 Nectar Street; and
the former dormitory located at 1725 17th Street.

subparagraph.heading: Hanford, washington.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Facilities, land, or interests in land on the Department of Energy Hanford Nuclear Reservation that are—

clause.content: the B Reactor National Historic Landmark;
the Hanford High School in the town of Hanford and Hanford Construction Camp Historic District;
the White Bluffs Bank building in the White Bluffs Historic District;
the warehouse at the Bruggemann’s Agricultural Complex;
the Hanford Irrigation District Pump House; and
the T Plant (221-T Process Building).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary and the Secretary of Energy (acting through the Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Richland site offices) shall enter into an agreement governing the respective roles of the Secretary and the Secretary of Energy in administering the facilities, land, or interests in land under the administrative jurisdiction of the Department of Energy that is to be included in the Historical Park under subsection (c)(2), including provisions for enhanced public access, management, interpretation, and historic preservation.

paragraph.heading: Responsibilities of the secretary.—
paragraph.chapeau: Any agreement under paragraph (1) shall provide that the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: have decisionmaking authority for the content of historic interpretation of the Manhattan Project for purposes of administering the Historical Park; and
ensure that the agreement provides an appropriate advisory role for the National Park Service in preserving the historic resources covered by the agreement.

paragraph.heading: Responsibilities of the secretary of energy.—
paragraph.chapeau: Any agreement under paragraph (1) shall provide that the Secretary of Energy—

subparagraph.content: shall ensure that the agreement appropriately protects public safety, national security, and other aspects of the ongoing mission of the Department of Energy at the Oak Ridge Reservation, Los Alamos National Laboratory, and Hanford Site;
may consult with and provide historical information to the Secretary concerning the Manhattan Project;

shall retain responsibility, in accordance with applicable law, for any environmental remediation or activities relating to structural safety that may be necessary in or around the facilities, land, or interests in land governed by the agreement; and
shall retain authority and legal obligations for historic preservation and general maintenance, including to ensure safe access, in connection with the Department’s Manhattan Project resources.

paragraph.heading: Amendments.—
paragraph.content: The agreement under paragraph (1) may be amended, including to add to the Historical Park facilities, land, or interests in land within the eligible areas described in subsection (c)(2) that are under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of Energy.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall consult with interested State, county, and local officials, organizations, and interested members of the public—

subparagraph.content: before executing any agreement under subsection (d); and
in the development of the general management plan under subsection (f)(2).

paragraph.heading: Notice of determination.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 30 days after the date on which an agreement under subsection (d) is entered into, the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register notice of the establishment of the Historical Park, including an official boundary map.

paragraph.heading: Availability of map.—
paragraph.content: The official boundary map published under paragraph (2) shall be on file and available for public inspection in the appropriate offices of the National Park Service. The map shall be updated to reflect any additions to the Historical Park from eligible areas described in subsection (c)(2).

paragraph.heading: Additions.—
paragraph.content: Any land, interest in land, or facility within the eligible areas described in subsection (c)(2) that is acquired by the Secretary or included in an amendment to the agreement under subsection (d)(4) shall be added to the Historical Park.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer the Historical Park in accordance with—

subparagraph.content: this section; and

subparagraph.chapeau: the laws generally applicable to units of the National Park System, including—

clause.content: the National Park System Organic Act (16 U.S.C. 1 et seq.); and
the Act of August 21, 1935 (16 U.S.C. 461 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: General management plan.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 3 years after the date on which funds are made available to carry out this subsection, the Secretary, with the concurrence of the Secretary of Energy, with respect to land administered by the Secretary of Energy, and in consultation and collaboration with the Oak Ridge, Los Alamos and Richland Department of Energy site offices, shall complete a general management plan for the Historical Park in accordance with section 12(b) of Public Law 91-383 (commonly known as the National Park Service General Authorities Act; 16 U.S.C. 1a-7(b)).

paragraph.heading: Interpretive tours.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may, subject to applicable law, provide interpretive tours of historically significant Manhattan Project sites and resources in the States of Tennessee, New Mexico, and Washington that are located outside the boundary of the Historical Park.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary may acquire land and interests in land within the eligible areas described in subsection (c)(2) by—

clause.content: transfer of administrative jurisdiction from the Department of Energy by agreement between the Secretary and the Secretary of Energy;
donation;
exchange; or
in the case of land and interests in land within the eligible areas described in subparagraphs (A) and (B) of subsection (c)(2), purchase from a willing seller.

subparagraph.heading: No use of condemnation.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may not acquire by condemnation any land or interest in land under this section.

subparagraph.heading: Facilities.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may acquire land or interests in land in the vicinity of the Historical Park for visitor and administrative facilities.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Secretary may enter into one or more agreements with the head of a Federal agency to provide public access to, and management, interpretation, and historic preservation of, historically significant Manhattan Project resources under the jurisdiction or control of the Federal agency.

clause.heading: Donations; cooperative agreements.—
clause.content: The Secretary may accept donations from, and enter into cooperative agreements with, State governments, units of local government, tribal governments, organizations, or individuals to further the purpose of an interagency agreement entered into under clause (i) or to provide visitor services and administrative facilities within reasonable proximity to the Historical Park.

subparagraph.heading: Technical assistance.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may provide technical assistance to State, local, or tribal governments, organizations, or individuals for the management, interpretation, and historic preservation of historically significant Manhattan Project resources not included within the Historical Park.

subparagraph.heading: Donations to department of energy.—
subparagraph.content: For the purposes of this section, or for the purpose of preserving and providing access to historically significant Manhattan Project resources, the Secretary of Energy may accept, hold, administer, and use gifts, bequests, and devises (including labor and services).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this section creates a protective perimeter or buffer zone around the boundary of the Historical Park.

paragraph.heading: Activities outside the boundary of the historical park.—
paragraph.content: The fact that an activity or use on land outside the boundary of the Historical Park can be seen or heard from within the boundary shall not preclude the activity or use outside the boundary of the Historical Park.

subsection.heading: No Cause of Action.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to create a cause of action with respect to activities outside or adjacent to the established boundary of the Historical Park.

section.heading: NORTH CASCADES NATIONAL PARK AND STEPHEN MATHER WILDERNESS.
section.content:
Title II of the Washington Park Wilderness Act of 1988 (16 U.S.C. 1132 note; Public Law 100-668) is amended by adding at the end the following:
“SEC. 207. [16 U.S.C. 1132 note] BOUNDARY ADJUSTMENTS FOR ROAD
“(a) In General.—The Secretary may adjust the boundaries of the North Cascades National Park and the Stephen Mather Wilderness in order to provide a 100-foot-wide corridor along which the Stehekin Valley Road may be rebuilt—
“(1) outside of the floodplain between milepost 12.9 and milepost 22.8;
“(2) within the boundaries of the North Cascades National Park; and
“(3) outside of the boundaries of the Stephen Mather Wilderness.
“(b) No Net Loss of Lands.—The boundary adjustments made under this section shall be such that equal acreage amounts are exchanged between the Stephen Mather Wilderness and the North Cascades National Park, resulting in no net loss of acreage to either the Stephen Mather Wilderness or the North Cascades National Park.”
.

section.heading: OREGON CAVES NATIONAL MONUMENT AND PRESERVE.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Map.—
paragraph.content: The term “map” means the map entitled “Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve”, numbered 150/80,023, and dated May 2010.

paragraph.heading: Monument.—
paragraph.content: The term “Monument” means the Oregon Caves National Monument established by Presidential Proclamation Number 876 (36 Stat. 2497), dated July 12, 1909.

paragraph.heading: National monument and preserve.—
paragraph.content: The term “National Monument and Preserve” means the Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve designated by subsection (b)(1)(A).

paragraph.heading: National preserve.—
paragraph.content: The term “National Preserve” means the National Preserve designated by subsection (b)(1)(B).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: Secretary concerned.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “Secretary concerned” means—

subparagraph.content: the Secretary of Agriculture (acting through the Chief of the Forest Service), with respect to National Forest System land; and
the Secretary of the Interior, with respect to land managed by the Bureau of Land Management.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of Oregon.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Monument and the National Preserve shall be administered as a single unit of the National Park System and collectively known and designated as the “Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve”.

subparagraph.heading: National preserve.—
subparagraph.content: The approximately 4,070 acres of land identified on the map as “Proposed Addition Lands” shall be designated as a National Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Administrative jurisdiction over the land designated as a National Preserve under paragraph (1)(B) is transferred from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary, to be administered as part of the National Monument and Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: Exclusion of land.—
subparagraph.content: The boundaries of the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest are adjusted to exclude the land transferred under subparagraph (A).

paragraph.heading: Boundary adjustment.—
paragraph.chapeau: The boundary of the National Monument and Preserve is modified to exclude approximately 4 acres of land—

subparagraph.content: located in the City of Cave Junction; and
identified on the map as the “Cave Junction Unit”.

paragraph.heading: Availability of map.—
paragraph.content: The map shall be on file and available for public inspection in the appropriate offices of the National Park Service.

paragraph.heading: References.—
paragraph.content: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the Monument shall be considered to be a reference to the “Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve”.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer the National Monument and Preserve in accordance with—

subparagraph.content: this section;
Presidential Proclamation Number 876 (36 Stat. 2497), dated July 12, 1909; and
any law (including regulations) generally applicable to units of the National Park System, including the National Park Service Organic Act (16 U.S.C. 1 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Fire management.—
paragraph.chapeau: As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, in accordance with paragraph (1), the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: revise the fire management plan for the Monument to include the land transferred under subsection (b)(2)(A); and
in accordance with the revised plan, carry out hazardous fuel management activities within the boundaries of the National Monument and Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

clause.content: allow for the completion of any Forest Service stewardship or service contract executed as of the date of enactment of this Act with respect to the National Preserve; and
recognize the authority of the Secretary of Agriculture for the purpose of administering a contract described in clause (i) through the completion of the contract.

subparagraph.heading: Terms and conditions.—
subparagraph.content: All terms and conditions of a contract described in subparagraph (A)(i) shall remain in place for the duration of the contract.

subparagraph.heading: Liability.—
subparagraph.content: The Forest Service shall be responsible for any liabilities relating to a contract described in subparagraph (A)(i).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), the Secretary may allow the grazing of livestock within the National Preserve to continue as authorized under permits or leases in existence as of the date of enactment of this Act.

subparagraph.heading: Applicable law.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Grazing under subparagraph (A) shall be—

clause.content: at a level not greater than the level at which the grazing exists as of the date of enactment of this Act, as measured in Animal Unit Months; and
in accordance with each applicable law (including National Park Service regulations).

paragraph.heading: Fish and wildlife.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall permit hunting and fishing on land and waters within the National Preserve in accordance with applicable Federal and State laws, except that the Secretary may, in consultation with the Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife, designate zones in which, and establish periods during which, no hunting or fishing shall be permitted for reasons of public safety, administration, or compliance by the Secretary with any applicable law (including regulations).

subsection.heading: Voluntary Grazing Lease or Permit Donation Program.—

subparagraph.heading: Acceptance by secretary concerned.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary concerned shall accept a grazing lease or permit that is donated by a lessee or permittee for—

clause.content: the Big Grayback Grazing Allotment located in the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest; and
the Billy Mountain Grazing Allotment located on a parcel of land that is managed by the Secretary (acting through the Director of the Bureau of Land Management).

subparagraph.heading: Termination.—
subparagraph.chapeau: With respect to each grazing permit or lease donated under subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall—

clause.content: terminate the grazing permit or lease; and
ensure a permanent end to grazing on the land covered by the grazing permit or lease.

paragraph.heading: Effect of donation.—
paragraph.content: A lessee or permittee that donates a grazing lease or grazing permit (or a portion of a grazing lease or grazing permit) under this section shall be considered to have waived any claim to any range improvement on the associated grazing allotment or portion of the associated grazing allotment, as applicable.

paragraph.heading: Designation.—
paragraph.content:
Section 3(a) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1274(a)) is amended by adding at the end the following:
“(208) River styx, oregon.—The subterranean segment of Cave Creek, known as the River Styx, to be administered by the Secretary of the Interior as a scenic river.” .

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content:
Section 5(a) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1276(a)) is amended by adding at the end the following:
“(141) Oregon caves national monument and preserve, oregon.—
“(A) Cave creek, oregon.—The 2.6-mile segment of Cave Creek from the headwaters at the River Styx to the boundary of the Rogue River Siskiyou National Forest.
“(B) Lake creek, oregon.—The 3.6-mile segment of Lake Creek from the headwaters at Bigelow Lakes to the confluence with Cave Creek.
“(C) No name creek, oregon.—The 0.6-mile segment of No Name Creek from the headwaters to the confluence with Cave Creek.
“(D) Panther creek.—The 0.8-mile segment of Panther Creek from the headwaters to the confluence with Lake Creek.
“(E) Upper cave creek.—The segment of Upper Cave Creek from the headwaters to the confluence with River Styx.”
.

subparagraph.heading: Study; report.—
subparagraph.content:
Section 5(b) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1276(b)) is amended by adding at the end the following:
“(20) Oregon caves national monument and preserve, oregon.—Not later than 3 years after the date on which funds are made available to carry out this paragraph, the Secretary shall—
“(A) complete the study of the Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve segments described in subsection (a)(141); and
“(B) submit to Congress a report containing the results of the study.”
.

section.heading: SAN ANTONIO MISSIONS NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK.
section.chapeau: Section 201 of Public Law 95-629 (16 U.S.C. 410ee) is amended—

by striking “Sec. 201. (a) In order” and inserting the following:
“SEC. 201. SAN ANTONIO MISSIONS NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK
“(a) Establishment.—
“(1) In general.—In order”
; and

subparagraph.content:
in the third sentence, by striking “After advising the” and inserting the following:
“(4) Revisions.—After advising the” ; and
