section.heading: VALLES CALDERA NATIONAL PRESERVE, NEW MEXICO.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Eligible employee.—
paragraph.content: The term “eligible employee” means a person who was a full-time or part-time employee of the Trust during the 180-day period immediately preceding the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Fund.—
paragraph.content: The term “Fund” means the Valles Caldera Fund established by section 106(h)(2) of the Valles Caldera Preservation Act (16 U.S.C. 698v-4(h)(2)).

paragraph.heading: Preserve.—
paragraph.content: The term “Preserve” means the Valles Caldera National Preserve in the State.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of New Mexico.

paragraph.heading: Trust.—
paragraph.content: The term “Trust” means the Valles Caldera Trust established by section 106(a) of the Valles Caldera Preservation Act (16 U.S.C. 698v-4(a)).

subsection.heading: Designation of Valles Caldera National Preserve as a Unit of the National Park System.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: To protect, preserve, and restore the fish, wildlife, watershed, natural, scientific, scenic, geologic, historic, cultural, archaeological, and recreational values of the area, the Valles Caldera National Preserve is designated as a unit of the National Park System.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The boundary of the Preserve shall consist of approximately 89,900 acres of land as depicted on the map entitled “Valles Caldera National Preserve Proposed Boundary”, numbered P80/102,036C, and dated November 4, 2014.

subparagraph.heading: Availability of map.—
subparagraph.content: The map described in subparagraph (A) shall be on file and available for public inspection in appropriate offices of the National Park Service.

subparagraph.heading: Applicable law.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer the Preserve in accordance with—

clause.content: this section; and

clause.chapeau: the laws generally applicable to units of the National Park System, including—

subclause.content: the National Park Service Organic Act (16 U.S.C. 1 et seq.); and
the Act of August 21, 1935 (16 U.S.C. 461 et seq.).

subparagraph.heading: Management coordination.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may coordinate the management and operations of the Preserve with the Bandelier National Monument.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Not later than 3 fiscal years after the date on which funds are made available to implement this subparagraph, the Secretary shall prepare a management plan for the Preserve.

clause.heading: Applicable law.—
clause.chapeau: The management plan shall be prepared in accordance with—

subclause.content: section 12(b) of Public Law 91-383 (commonly known as the “National Park Service General Authorities Act”) (16 U.S.C. 1a-7(b)); and
any other applicable laws.

clause.heading: Consultation.—
clause.chapeau: The management plan shall be prepared in consultation with—

subclause.content: the Secretary of Agriculture;
State and local governments;
Indian tribes and pueblos, including the Pueblos of Jemez, Santa Clara, and San Ildefonso; and
the public.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary may acquire land and interests in land within the boundaries of the Preserve by—

clause.content: purchase from a willing seller with donated or appropriated funds; or
donation.

subparagraph.heading: Prohibition of condemnation.—
subparagraph.content: No land or interest in land within the boundaries of the Preserve may be acquired by condemnation.

subparagraph.heading: Administration of acquired land.—
subparagraph.content: On acquisition of any land or interests in land under subparagraph (A), the acquired land or interests in land shall be administered as part of the Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

clause.content: until the date on which a management plan is completed in accordance with paragraph (3)(C), carry out the science and education program for the Preserve established by the Trust; and

clause.chapeau: beginning on the date on which a management plan is completed in accordance with paragraph (3)(C), establish a science and education program for the Preserve that—

subclause.content: allows for research and interpretation of the natural, historic, cultural, geologic and other scientific features of the Preserve;
provides for improved methods of ecological restoration and science-based adaptive management of the Preserve; and
promotes outdoor educational experiences in the Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: Science and education center.—
subparagraph.content: As part of the program established under subparagraph (A)(ii), the Secretary may establish a science and education center outside the boundaries of the Preserve in Jemez Springs, New Mexico.

paragraph.heading: Grazing.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall allow the grazing of livestock within the Preserve to continue—

subparagraph.content: at levels and locations determined by the Secretary to be appropriate, consistent with this section; and
to the extent the use furthers scientific research or interpretation of the ranching history of the Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the Secretary shall permit hunting, fishing, and trapping on land and water within the Preserve in accordance with applicable Federal and State law.

subparagraph.heading: Administrative exceptions.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may designate areas in which, and establish limited periods during which, no hunting, fishing, or trapping shall be permitted under subparagraph (A) for reasons of public safety, administration, or compliance with applicable law.

subparagraph.heading: Agency agreement.—
subparagraph.content: Except in an emergency, regulations closing areas within the Preserve to hunting, fishing, or trapping under this paragraph shall be made in consultation with the appropriate agency of the State having responsibility for fish and wildlife administration.

subparagraph.heading: Savings clause.—
subparagraph.content: Nothing in this section affects any jurisdiction or responsibility of the State with respect to fish and wildlife in the Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall undertake activities to improve the health of forest, grassland, and riparian areas within the Preserve, including any activities carried out in accordance with title IV of the Omnibus Public Land Management Act of 2009 (16 U.S.C. 7301 et seq.).

subparagraph.heading: Agreements.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may enter into agreements with adjacent pueblos to coordinate activities carried out under subparagraph (A) on the Preserve and adjacent pueblo land.

paragraph.heading: Withdrawal.—
paragraph.chapeau: Subject to valid existing rights, all land and interests in land within the boundaries of the Preserve are withdrawn from—

subparagraph.content: entry, disposal, or appropriation under the public land laws;
location, entry, and patent under the mining laws; and
operation of the mineral leasing laws, geothermal leasing laws, and mineral materials laws.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Except as provided in subparagraph (C), for the purposes of preserving the natural, cultural, religious, archaeological, and historic resources of the volcanic domes and other peaks in the Preserve described in subparagraph (B) within the area of the domes and peaks above 9,600 feet in elevation or 250 feet below the top of the dome, whichever is lower—

clause.content: no roads or buildings shall be constructed; and
no motorized access shall be allowed.

subparagraph.heading: Description of volcanic domes.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The volcanic domes and other peaks referred to in subparagraph (A) are—

clause.content: Redondo Peak;
Redondito;
South Mountain;
San Antonio Mountain;
Cerro Seco;
Cerro San Luis;
Cerros Santa Rosa;
Cerros del Abrigo;
Cerro del Medio;
Rabbit Mountain;
Cerro Grande;
Cerro Toledo;
Indian Point;
Sierra de los Valles; and
Cerros de los Posos.

subparagraph.heading: Exception.—
subparagraph.content: Subparagraph (A) shall not apply in cases in which construction or motorized access is necessary for administrative purposes (including ecological restoration activities or measures required in emergencies to protect the health and safety of persons in the area).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary, in consultation with Indian tribes and pueblos, shall ensure the protection of traditional cultural and religious sites in the Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: Access.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary, in accordance with Public Law 95-341 (commonly known as the “American Indian Religious Freedom Act”) (42 U.S.C. 1996)—

clause.content: shall provide access to the sites described in subparagraph (A) by members of Indian tribes or pueblos for traditional cultural and customary uses; and

may, on request of an Indian tribe or pueblo, temporarily close to general public use 1 or more specific areas of the Preserve to protect traditional cultural and customary uses in the area by members of the Indian tribe or pueblo.

subparagraph.heading: Prohibition on motorized access.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall maintain prohibitions on the use of motorized or mechanized travel on Preserve land located adjacent to the Santa Clara Indian Reservation, to the extent the prohibition was in effect on the date of enactment of this Act.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Agriculture, affected Indian tribes and pueblos, and the public, shall study the feasibility of establishing a hiking trail along the rim of the Valles Caldera on—

clause.content: land within the Preserve; and
National Forest System land that is adjacent to the Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: Agreements.—
subparagraph.chapeau: On the request of an affected Indian tribe or pueblo, the Secretary and the Secretary of Agriculture shall seek to enter into an agreement with the Indian tribe or pueblo with respect to the Caldera Rim Trail that provides for the protection of—

clause.content: cultural and religious sites in the vicinity of the trail; and
the privacy of adjacent pueblo land.

paragraph.heading: Valid existing rights.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this section affects valid existing rights.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Administrative jurisdiction over the Preserve is transferred from the Secretary of Agriculture and the Trust to the Secretary, to be administered as a unit of the National Park System, in accordance with subsection (b).

paragraph.heading: Exclusion from santa fe national forest.—
paragraph.content: The boundaries of the Santa Fe National Forest are modified to exclude the Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: Memorandum of agreement.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary and the Trust shall enter into a memorandum of agreement to facilitate the orderly transfer to the Secretary of the administration of the Preserve.

subparagraph.heading: Existing management plans.—
subparagraph.content: Notwithstanding the repeal made by subsection (d)(1), until the date on which the Secretary completes a management plan for the Preserve in accordance with subsection (b)(3)(C), the Secretary may administer the Preserve in accordance with any management activities or plans adopted by the Trust under the Valles Caldera Preservation Act (16 U.S.C. 698v et seq.), to the extent the activities or plans are consistent with subsection (b)(3)(A).

subparagraph.heading: Public use.—
subparagraph.content: The Preserve shall remain open to public use during the interim management period, subject to such terms and conditions as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

subparagraph.heading: Termination.—
subparagraph.content: The Trust shall terminate 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act unless the Secretary determines that the termination date should be extended to facilitate the transitional management of the Preserve.

clause.heading: Assets.—
clause.chapeau: On termination of the Trust—

subclause.content: all assets of the Trust shall be transferred to the Secretary; and
any amounts appropriated for the Trust shall remain available to the Secretary for the administration of the Preserve.

subclause.heading: In general.—
subclause.content: On termination of the Trust, the Secretary shall assume all contracts, obligations, and other liabilities of the Trust.

item.heading: Budget.—
item.content: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary and the Trust shall prepare a budget for the interim management of the Preserve.

item.heading: Written concurrence required.—
item.content: The Trust shall not incur any new liabilities not authorized in the budget prepared under item (aa) without the written concurrence of the Secretary.

clause.heading: Hiring.—
clause.content: The Secretary and the Secretary of Agriculture may hire employees of the Trust on a noncompetitive basis for comparable positions at the Preserve or other areas or offices under the jurisdiction of the Secretary or the Secretary of Agriculture.

clause.heading: Salary.—
clause.content: Any employees hired from the Trust under clause (i) shall be subject to the provisions of chapter 51, and subchapter III of chapter 53, title 5, United States Code, relating to classification and General Schedule pay rates.

clause.heading: Interim retention of eligible employees.—
clause.chapeau: For a period of not less than 180 days beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, all eligible employees of the Trust shall be—

subclause.content: retained in the employment of the Trust;
considered to be placed on detail to the Secretary; and
subject to the direction of the Secretary.

clause.heading: Termination for cause.—
clause.content: Nothing in this subparagraph precludes the termination of employment of an eligible employee for cause during the period described in clause (iii).

subparagraph.heading: Records.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall have access to all records of the Trust pertaining to the management of the Preserve.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Effective on the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall assume the powers of the Trust over the Fund.

clause.heading: Availability and use.—
clause.content: Any amounts in the Fund as of the date of enactment of this Act shall be available to the Secretary for use, without further appropriation, for the management of the Preserve.

subsection.heading: Repeal of Valles Caldera Preservation Act.—

paragraph.heading: Repeal.—
paragraph.content: On the termination of the Trust, the Valles Caldera Preservation Act (16 U.S.C. 698v et seq.) is repealed.

paragraph.heading: Effect of repeal.—
paragraph.chapeau: Notwithstanding the repeal made by paragraph (1)—

subparagraph.content: the authority of the Secretary of Agriculture to acquire mineral interests under section 104(e) of the Valles Caldera Preservation Act (16 U.S.C. 698v-2(e)) is transferred to the Secretary and any proceeding for the condemnation of, or payment of compensation for, an outstanding mineral interest pursuant to the transferred authority shall continue;
the provisions in section 104(g) of the Valles Caldera Preservation Act (16 U.S.C. 698v-2(g)) relating to the Pueblo of Santa Clara shall remain in effect; and
the Fund shall not be terminated until all amounts in the Fund have been expended by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Boundaries.—
paragraph.chapeau: The repeal of the Valles Caldera Preservation Act (16 U.S.C. 698v et seq.) shall not affect the boundaries as of the date of enactment of this Act (including maps and legal descriptions) of—

subparagraph.content: the Preserve;
the Santa Fe National Forest (other than the modification made by subsection (c)(2));
Bandelier National Monument; and
any land conveyed to the Pueblo of Santa Clara.

section.heading: VICKSBURG NATIONAL MILITARY PARK.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary of the Interior (referred to in this section as the “Secretary”) may acquire the land or any interests in land within the area identified as “Modified Core Battlefield” for the Port Gibson Unit, the Champion Hill Unit, and the Raymond Unit as generally depicted on the map entitled “Vicksburg National Military Park—Proposed Battlefield Additions”, numbered 306/100986A (4 sheets), and dated July 2012.

paragraph.heading: Methods of acquisition.—
paragraph.content: Land may be acquired under paragraph (1) by donation, purchase with donated or appropriated funds, or exchange, except that land owned by the State of Mississippi or any political subdivisions of the State may be acquired only by donation.

subsection.heading: Availability of Map.—
subsection.content: The map described in subsection (a)(1) shall be on file and available for public inspection in the appropriate offices of the National Park Service.

subsection.heading: Boundary Adjustment.—
subsection.chapeau: On the acquisition of land by the Secretary under this section—

paragraph.content: the acquired land shall be added to Vicksburg National Military Park;
the boundary of the Vicksburg National Military Park shall be adjusted to reflect the acquisition of the land; and
the acquired land shall be administered as part of the Vicksburg National Military Park in accordance with applicable laws (including regulations).

section.heading: SPECIAL RESOURCE STUDIES.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of the Interior (referred to in this section as the “Secretary”) shall conduct a special resource study regarding each area, site, and issue identified in subsection (b) to evaluate—

paragraph.content: the national significance of the area, site, or issue; and
the suitability and feasibility of designating such an area or site as a unit of the National Park System.

subsection.heading: Studies.—
subsection.chapeau: The areas, sites, and issues referred to in subsection (a) are the following:

paragraph.heading: Lower mississippi river, louisiana.—
paragraph.content: Sites along the lower Mississippi River in the State of Louisiana, including Fort St. Philip, Fort Jackson, the Head of Passes, and any related and supporting historical, cultural, or recreational resource located in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana.

paragraph.heading: Buffalo soldiers.—
paragraph.content: The role of the Buffalo Soldiers in the early years of the National Park System, including an evaluation of appropriate ways to enhance historical research, education, interpretation, and public awareness of the story of the stewardship role of the Buffalo Soldiers in the National Parks, including ways to link the story to the development of National Parks and the story of African-American military service following the Civil War.

paragraph.heading: Rota, commonwealth of northern mariana islands.—
paragraph.content: Prehistoric, historic, and limestone forest sites on the island of Rota, Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.

paragraph.heading: Prison ship monument, new york.—
paragraph.content: The Prison Ship Martyrs’ Monument in Fort Greene Park, Brooklyn, New York.

paragraph.heading: Flushing remonstrance, new york.—
paragraph.content: The John Bowne House, located at 3701 Bowne Street, Queens, New York, the Friends Meeting House located at 137-17 Northern Boulevard, Queens, New York, and other resources in the vicinity of Flushing, New York, relating to the history of religious freedom during the era of the signing of the Flushing Remonstrance.

paragraph.heading: West hunter street baptist church, georgia.—
paragraph.content: The historic West Hunter Street Baptist Church, located at 775 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, SW, Atlanta, Georgia, and the block on which the church is located.

paragraph.heading: Mill springs battlefield, kentucky.—
paragraph.content: The area encompassed by the National Historic Landmark designations relating to the 1862 Battle of Mill Springs located in Pulaski and Wayne Counties in the State of Kentucky.

paragraph.heading: New philadelphia, illinois.—
paragraph.content: The New Philadelphia archeological site and surrounding land in the State of Illinois.

subsection.heading: Criteria.—
subsection.content: In conducting a study under this section, the Secretary shall use the criteria for the study of areas for potential inclusion in the National Park System described in section 8(c) of Public Law 91-383 (commonly known as the “National Park System General Authorities Act”) (16 U.S.C. 1a-5(c)).

subsection.heading: Contents.—
subsection.chapeau: Each study authorized by this section shall—

paragraph.content: determine the suitability and feasibility of designating the applicable area or site as a unit of the National Park System;
include cost estimates for any necessary acquisition, development, operation, and maintenance of the applicable area or site;

paragraph.chapeau: include an analysis of the effect of the applicable area or site on—

subparagraph.content: existing commercial and recreational activities;
the authorization, construction, operation, maintenance, or improvement of energy production and transmission or other infrastructure in the area; and
the authority of State and local governments to manage those activities;

paragraph.content: include an identification of any authorities, including condemnation, that will compel or permit the Secretary to influence or participate in local land use decisions (such as zoning) or place restrictions on non-Federal land if the applicable area or site is designated as a unit of the National Park System; and
identify alternatives for the management, administration, and protection of the applicable area or site.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 3 years after the date on which funds are made available to carry out a study authorized by this section, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate a report the describes—

paragraph.content: the findings and recommendations of the study; and
any applicable recommendations of the Secretary.

section.heading: NATIONAL HISTORIC SITE SUPPORT FACILITY IMPROVEMENTS.

subsection.heading: Improvement.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service (referred to in this section as the “Secretary”), may make improvements to a support facility, including a visitor center, for a National Historic Site operated by the National Park Service if the project—

paragraph.content: is conducted using amounts included in the budget of the National Park Service in effect on the date on which the project is authorized;
is subject to a 50 percent non-Federal cost-sharing requirement; and
is conducted in an area in which the National Park Service was authorized by law in effect before the date of enactment of this Act to establish a support facility.

subsection.heading: Operation and Use.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may operate and use all or part of a support facility, including a visitor center, for a National Historic Site operated by the National Park Service—

paragraph.content: to carry out duties associated with operating and supporting the National Historic Site; and
only in accordance with an agreement between the Secretary and the unit of local government in which the support facility is located.

section.heading: NATIONAL PARK SYSTEM DONOR ACKNOWLEDGMENT.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Donor acknowledgment.—
paragraph.content: The term “donor acknowledgment” means an appropriate statement or credit acknowledging a donation.

paragraph.heading: National park system.—
paragraph.content: The term “National Park System” includes each program and individual unit of the National Park System.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

subsection.heading: Donor Acknowledgments in Units of National Park System.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary may authorize a donor acknowledgment to recognize a donation to—

subparagraph.content: the National Park Service; or
the National Park System.

paragraph.heading: Restrictions.—
paragraph.chapeau: A donor acknowledgment shall not be used to state or imply—

subparagraph.content: recognition of the donor or any product or service of the donor as an official sponsor, or any similar form of recognition, of the National Park Service or the National Park System;
a National Park Service endorsement of the donor or any product or service of the donor; or
naming rights to any unit of the National Park System or a National Park System facility, including a visitor center.

subparagraph.heading: Display.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A donor acknowledgment shall be displayed—

clause.content: in a manner that is approved by the Secretary; and
for a period of time, as determined by the Secretary, that is commensurate with the amount of the contribution and the life of the structure.

subparagraph.heading: Guidelines.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall establish donor acknowledgment guidelines that take into account the unique requirements of individual units and programs of the National Park System.

subparagraph.heading: Use of slogans prohibited.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A donor acknowledgment shall not permit the use of—

clause.content: an advertising slogan; or
a statement or credit promoting or opposing a political candidate or issue.

subparagraph.heading: Visitor and administrative facilities.—
subparagraph.content: A donor acknowledgment may be located on or inside a visitor center or administrative facility of the National Park System (including in a specific room or section) or any other appropriate location, such as on a donor recognition wall or plaque.

subparagraph.heading: Outside.—
subparagraph.content: A donor acknowledgment may be located in an area outside of a visitor or administrative facility described in subparagraph (A), including a bench, brick, pathway, area of landscaping, or plaza.

subparagraph.heading: Projects.—
subparagraph.content: A donor acknowledgment may be located near a park construction or restoration project, if the donation directly relates to the project.

subparagraph.heading: Vehicles.—
subparagraph.content: A donor acknowledgment may be placed on a National Park Service vehicle, if the donation directly relates to the vehicle.

subparagraph.heading: Limitation.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Any donor acknowledgment associated with a historic structure or placed outside a park restoration project—

clause.content: shall be freestanding; and
shall not obstruct a natural or historical site or view.

paragraph.heading: Printed, digital, and media platforms.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may authorize the use of donor acknowledgments under this subsection to include donor acknowledgments on printed, digital, and media platforms, including brochures or Internet websites relating to a specific unit of the National Park System.

subsection.heading: Commemorative Works Act Amendments.—
subsection.chapeau: Section 8905 of title 40, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.content: in subsection (b), by striking paragraph (7); and

by adding at the end the following:
“(c) Donor Contributions.—
“(1) Acknowledgment of donor contribution.—Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the Secretary of the Interior or Administrator of General Services, as applicable, may permit a sponsor to acknowledge donor contributions at the commemorative work.
“(2) Requirements.—An acknowledgment under paragraph (1) shall—
“(A) be displayed—
“(i) inside an ancillary structure associated with the commemorative work; or
“(ii) as part of a manmade landscape feature at the commemorative work; and
“(B) conform to applicable National Park Service or General Services Administration guidelines for donor recognition, as applicable.
“(3) Limitations.—An acknowledgment under paragraph (1) shall—
“(A) be limited to an appropriate statement or credit recognizing the contribution;
“(B) be displayed in a form in accordance with National Park Service and General Services Administration guidelines;
“(C) be displayed for a period of up to 10 years, with the display period to be commensurate with the level of the contribution, as determined in accordance with the plan and guidelines described in subparagraph (B);
“(D) be freestanding; and
“(E) not be affixed to—
“(i) any landscape feature at the commemorative work; or
“(ii) any object in a museum collection.
“(4) Cost.—The sponsor shall bear all expenses related to the display of donor acknowledgments under paragraph (1).
“(5) Applicability.—This subsection shall apply to any commemorative work dedicated after January 1, 2010.”
.

subsection.heading: Effect of Section.—
subsection.chapeau: Nothing in this section or an amendment made by this section—

paragraph.content: requires the Secretary to accept a donation; or
modifies section 145 of Public Law 108-108 (16 U.S.C. 1a-1 note; 117 Stat. 1280).

section.heading: COIN TO COMMEMORATE 100TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE NATIONAL PARK SERVICE.

paragraph.heading: Denominations.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary of the Treasury (in this section referred to as the “Secretary”) shall mint and issue the following coins:

subparagraph.heading: $5 GOLD COINS.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not more than 100,000 $5 coins, which shall—

clause.content: weigh 8.359 grams;
have a diameter of 0.850 inches; and
contain 90 percent gold and 10 percent alloy.

subparagraph.heading: $1 SILVER COINS.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not more than 500,000 $1 coins, which shall—

clause.content: weigh 26.73 grams;
have a diameter of 1.500 inches; and
contain 90 percent silver and 10 percent copper.

subparagraph.heading: Half dollar clad coins.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not more than 750,000 half dollar coins, which shall—

clause.content: weigh 11.34 grams;
have a diameter of 1.205 inches; and
be minted to the specifications for half dollar coins, contained in section 5112(b) of title 31, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Legal tender.—
paragraph.content: The coins minted under this section shall be legal tender, as provided in section 5103 of title 31, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Numismatic items.—
paragraph.content: For purposes of sections 5134 and 5136 of title 31, United States Code, all coins minted under this section shall be considered to be numismatic items.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The design of the coins minted under this section shall be emblematic of the 100th anniversary of the National Park Service.

subparagraph.heading: Designation and inscriptions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: On each coin minted under this section there shall be—

clause.content: a designation of the face value of the coin;
an inscription of the year “2016”; and
inscriptions of the words “Liberty”, “In God We Trust”, “United States of America”, and “E Pluribus Unum”.

paragraph.heading: Selection.—
paragraph.chapeau: The design for the coins minted under this section shall be—

subparagraph.chapeau: selected by the Secretary after consultation with—

clause.content: the National Park Service;
the National Park Foundation; and
the Commission of Fine Arts; and

subparagraph.content: reviewed by the Citizens Coinage Advisory Committee.

paragraph.heading: Quality of coins.—
paragraph.content: Coins minted under this section shall be issued in uncirculated and proof qualities.

paragraph.heading: Period for issuance.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may issue coins minted under this section only during the period beginning on January 1, 2016, and ending on December 31, 2016.

paragraph.heading: Sale price.—
paragraph.chapeau: The coins issued under this section shall be sold by the Secretary at a price equal to the sum of—

subparagraph.content: the face value of the coins;
the surcharge provided in subsection (e)(1) with respect to the coins; and
the cost of designing and issuing the coins (including labor, materials, dies, use of machinery, overhead expenses, marketing, and shipping).

paragraph.heading: Bulk sales.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall make bulk sales of the coins issued under this section at a reasonable discount.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall accept prepaid orders for the coins minted under this section before the issuance of such coins.

subparagraph.heading: Discount.—
subparagraph.content: Sale prices with respect to prepaid orders under subparagraph (A) shall be at a reasonable discount.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: All sales of coins minted under this section shall include a surcharge as follows:

subparagraph.content: A surcharge of $35 per coin for the $5 coin.
A surcharge of $10 per coin for the $1 coin.
A surcharge of $5 per coin for the half dollar coin.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to section 5134(f) of title 31, United States Code, all surcharges which are received by the Secretary from the sale of coins issued under this section shall be promptly paid by the Secretary to the National Park Foundation for projects and programs that help preserve and protect resources under the stewardship of the National Park Service and promote public enjoyment and appreciation of those resources.

subparagraph.heading: Prohibition on land acquisition.—
subparagraph.content: Surcharges paid to the National Park Foundation pursuant to subparagraph (A) may not be used for land acquisition.

paragraph.heading: Audits.—
paragraph.content: The National Park Foundation shall be subject to the audit requirements of section 5134(f)(2) of title 31, United States Code, with regard to the amounts received by the Foundation under paragraph (2).

paragraph.heading: Limitations.—
paragraph.content: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), no surcharge may be included with respect to the issuance under this section of any coin during a calendar year if, as of the time of such issuance, the issuance of such coin would result in the number of commemorative coin programs issued during such year to exceed the annual 2 commemorative coin program issuance limitation under section 5112(m)(1) of title 31, United States Code (as in effect on the date of the enactment of this Act). The Secretary of the Treasury may issue guidance to carry out this paragraph.

subsection.heading: Financial Assurances.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that—

paragraph.content: minting and issuing coins under this section will not result in any net cost to the United States Government; and

no funds, including applicable surcharges, shall be disbursed to any recipient designated in subsection (e) until the total cost of designing and issuing all of the coins authorized by this section (including labor, materials, dies, use of machinery, overhead expenses, marketing, and shipping) is recovered by the United States Treasury, consistent with sections 5112(m) and 5134(f) of title 31, United States Code.

subsection.heading: Budget Compliance.—
subsection.content: The budgetary effects of this section, for the purpose of complying with the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010, shall be determined by reference to the latest statement titled “Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation” for this section, submitted for printing in the Congressional Record by the Chairman of the Committee on the Budget of the House of Representatives, provided that such statement has been submitted prior to the vote on passage.

section.heading: COMMISSION TO STUDY THE POTENTIAL CREATION OF A NATIONAL WOMEN’S HISTORY MUSEUM.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Commission.—
paragraph.content: The term “Commission” means the Commission to Study the Potential Creation of a National Women’s History Museum established by subsection (b)(1).

paragraph.heading: Museum.—
paragraph.content: The term “Museum” means the National Women’s History Museum.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: There is established the Commission to Study the Potential Creation of a National Women’s History Museum.

paragraph.heading: Membership.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Commission shall be composed of 8 members, of whom—

subparagraph.content: 2 members shall be appointed by the majority leader of the Senate;
2 members shall be appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives;
2 members shall be appointed by the minority leader of the Senate; and
2 members shall be appointed by the minority leader of the House of Representatives.

paragraph.heading: Qualifications.—
paragraph.chapeau: Members of the Commission shall be appointed to the Commission from among individuals, or representatives of institutions or entities, who possess—

clause.content: a demonstrated commitment to the research, study, or promotion of women’s history, art, political or economic status, or culture; and

subclause.content: expertise in museum administration;
expertise in fundraising for nonprofit or cultural institutions;
experience in the study and teaching of women’s history;
experience in studying the issue of the representation of women in art, life, history, and culture at the Smithsonian Institution; or
extensive experience in public or elected service;

subparagraph.content: experience in the administration of, or the planning for, the establishment of, museums; or
experience in the planning, design, or construction of museum facilities.

paragraph.heading: Prohibition.—
paragraph.content: No employee of the Federal Government may serve as a member of the Commission.

paragraph.heading: Deadline for initial appointment.—
paragraph.content: The initial members of the Commission shall be appointed not later than the date that is 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Vacancies.—
paragraph.chapeau: A vacancy in the Commission—

subparagraph.content: shall not affect the powers of the Commission; and
shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment was made.

paragraph.heading: Chairperson.—
paragraph.content: The Commission shall, by majority vote of all of the members, select 1 member of the Commission to serve as the Chairperson of the Commission.

subparagraph.heading: Plan of action.—
subparagraph.content: The Commission shall submit to the President and Congress a report containing the recommendations of the Commission with respect to a plan of action for the establishment and maintenance of a National Women’s History Museum in Washington, DC.

subparagraph.heading: Report on issues.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Commission shall submit to the President and Congress a report that addresses the following issues:

clause.content: The availability and cost of collections to be acquired and housed in the Museum.
The impact of the Museum on regional women history-related museums.
Potential locations for the Museum in Washington, DC, and its environs.
Whether the Museum should be part of the Smithsonian Institution.
The governance and organizational structure from which the Museum should operate.
Best practices for engaging women in the development and design of the Museum.
The cost of constructing, operating, and maintaining the Museum.

subparagraph.heading: Deadline.—
subparagraph.content: The reports required under subparagraphs (A) and (B) shall be submitted not later than the date that is 18 months after the date of the first meeting of the Commission.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Commission shall develop a fundraising plan to support the establishment, operation, and maintenance of the Museum through contributions from the public.

subparagraph.heading: Considerations.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In developing the fundraising plan under subparagraph (A), the Commission shall consider—

clause.content: the role of the National Women’s History Museum (a nonprofit, educational organization described in section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 that was incorporated in 1996 in Washington, DC, and dedicated for the purpose of establishing a women’s history museum) in raising funds for the construction of the Museum; and
issues relating to funding the operations and maintenance of the Museum in perpetuity without reliance on appropriations of Federal funds.

subparagraph.heading: Independent review.—
subparagraph.content: The Commission shall obtain an independent review of the viability of the plan developed under subparagraph (A) and such review shall include an analysis as to whether the plan is likely to achieve the level of resources necessary to fund the construction of the Museum and the operations and maintenance of the Museum in perpetuity without reliance on appropriations of Federal funds.

subparagraph.heading: Submission.—
subparagraph.content: The Commission shall submit the plan developed under subparagraph (A) and the review conducted under subparagraph (C) to the Committees on Transportation and Infrastructure, House Administration, Natural Resources, and Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Committees on Rules and Administration, Energy and Natural Resources, and Appropriations of the Senate.

paragraph.heading: Legislation to carry out plan of action.—
paragraph.content: Based on the recommendations contained in the report submitted under subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (1), the Commission shall submit for consideration to the Committees on Transportation and Infrastructure, House Administration, Natural Resources, and Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Committees on Rules and Administration, Energy and Natural Resources, and Appropriations of the Senate recommendations for a legislative plan of action to establish and construct the Museum.

paragraph.heading: National conference.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 18 months after the date on which the initial members of the Commission are appointed under subsection (b), the Commission may, in carrying out the duties of the Commission under this subsection, convene a national conference relating to the Museum, to be comprised of individuals committed to the advancement of the life, art, history, and culture of women.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Commission may employ and compensate an executive director and any other additional personnel that are necessary to enable the Commission to perform the duties of the Commission.

subparagraph.heading: Rates of pay.—
subparagraph.content: Rates of pay for persons employed under subparagraph (A) shall be consistent with the rates of pay allowed for employees of a temporary organization under section 3161 of title 5, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Not federal employment.—
paragraph.content: Any individual employed under this section shall not be considered a Federal employee for the purpose of any law governing Federal employment.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), on request of the Commission, the head of a Federal agency may provide technical assistance to the Commission.

subparagraph.heading: Prohibition.—
subparagraph.content: No Federal employees may be detailed to the Commission.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A member of the Commission—

clause.content: shall not be considered to be a Federal employee for any purpose by reason of service on the Commission; and
shall serve without pay.

subparagraph.heading: Travel expenses.—
subparagraph.content: A member of the Commission shall be allowed a per diem allowance for travel expenses, at rates consistent with those authorized under subchapter I of chapter 57 of title 5, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Gifts, bequests, devises.—
paragraph.content: The Commission may solicit, accept, use, and dispose of gifts, bequests, or devises of money, services, or real or personal property for the purpose of aiding or facilitating the work of the Commission.

paragraph.heading: Federal advisory committee act.—
paragraph.content: The Commission shall not be subject to the Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.).

subsection.heading: Termination.—
subsection.content: The Commission shall terminate on the date that is 30 days after the date on which the final versions of the reports required under section (c)(1) are submitted.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Commission shall be solely responsible for acceptance of contributions for, and payment of the expenses of, the Commission.

paragraph.heading: Prohibition.—
paragraph.content: No Federal funds may be obligated to carry out this section.

section.heading: CAPE HATTERAS NATIONAL SEASHORE RECREATIONAL AREA.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Final rule.—
paragraph.content: The term “Final Rule” means the final rule entitled “Special Regulations, Areas of the National Park System, Cape Hatteras National Seashore—Off-Road Vehicle Management” (77 Fed. Reg. 3123 (January 23, 2012)).

paragraph.heading: National seashore.—
paragraph.content: The term “National Seashore” means the Cape Hatteras National Seashore Recreational Area.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of North Carolina.

subsection.heading: Review and Adjustment of Wildlife Protection Buffers.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall review and modify wildlife buffers in the National Seashore in accordance with this subsection and any other applicable law.

paragraph.heading: Buffer modifications.—
paragraph.chapeau: In modifying wildlife buffers under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall, using adaptive management practices—

subparagraph.content: ensure that the buffers are of the shortest duration and cover the smallest area necessary to protect a species, as determined in accordance with peer-reviewed scientific data; and
designate pedestrian and vehicle corridors around areas of the National Seashore closed because of wildlife buffers, to allow access to areas that are open.

paragraph.heading: Coordination with state.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary, after coordinating with the State, shall determine appropriate buffer protections for species that are not listed under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (16 U.S.C. 1531 et seq.), but that are identified for protection under State law.

subsection.heading: Modifications to Final Rule.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall undertake a public process to consider, consistent with management requirements at the National Seashore, the following changes to the Final Rule:

paragraph.content: Opening beaches at the National Seashore that are closed to night driving restrictions, by opening beach segments each morning on a rolling basis as daily management reviews are completed.
Extending seasonal off-road vehicle routes for additional periods in the Fall and Spring if off-road vehicle use would not create resource management problems at the National Seashore.
Modifying the size and location of vehicle-free areas.

subsection.heading: Construction of New Vehicle Access Points.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall construct new vehicle access points and roads at the National Seashore—

paragraph.content: as expeditiously as practicable; and
in accordance with applicable management plans for the National Seashore.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall report to Congress within 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act on measures taken to implement this section.

section.heading: ALPINE LAKES WILDERNESS ADDITIONS AND PRATT AND MIDDLE FORK SNOQUALMIE RIVERS PROTECTION.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: There is designated as wilderness and as a component of the National Wilderness Preservation System certain Federal land in the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest in the State of Washington comprising approximately 22,173 acres that is within the Proposed Alpine Lakes Wilderness Additions Boundary, as generally depicted on the map entitled “Proposed Alpine Lakes Wilderness Additions” and dated December 3, 2009, which is incorporated in and shall be considered to be a part of the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.

subparagraph.heading: Management.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to valid existing rights, the land designated as wilderness by paragraph (1) shall be administered by the Secretary of Agriculture (referred to in this section as the “Secretary”), in accordance with the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1131 et seq.), except that any reference in that Act to the effective date of that Act shall be considered to be a reference to the date of enactment of this Act.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall file a map and a legal description of the land designated as wilderness by paragraph (1) with—

subclause.content: the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives; and
the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate.

clause.heading: Force of law.—
clause.content: A map and legal description filed under clause (i) shall have the same force and effect as if included in this section, except that the Secretary may correct minor errors in the map and legal description.

clause.heading: Public availability.—
clause.content: The map and legal description filed under clause (i) shall be filed and made available for public inspection in the appropriate office of the Forest Service.

paragraph.heading: Incorporation of acquired land and interests in land.—
paragraph.chapeau: Any land or interests in land within the Proposed Alpine Lakes Wilderness Additions Boundary, as generally depicted on the map entitled “Proposed Alpine Lakes Wilderness Additions” and dated December 3, 2009, that is acquired by the United States shall—

subparagraph.content: become part of the wilderness area; and
be managed in accordance with paragraph (2)(A).

paragraph.heading: Designation.—
paragraph.content:
Section 3(a) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1274(a)) is amended by inserting after paragraph (208), as added by section 3040(e), the following:
“(209) Middle fork snoqualmie, washington.—The 27.4-mile segment from the headwaters of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River near La Bohn Gap in NE ¼ sec. 20, T. 24 N., R. 13 E., to the northern boundary of sec. 11, T. 23 N., R. 9 E., to be administered by the Secretary of Agriculture in the following classifications:
“(A) The approximately 6.4-mile segment from the headwaters of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River near La Bohn Gap in NE ¼ sec. 20, T. 24 N., R. 13 E., to the west section line of sec. 3, T. 23 N., R. 12 E., as a wild river.
“(B) The approximately 21-mile segment from the west section line of sec. 3, T. 23 N., R. 12 E., to the northern boundary of sec. 11, T. 23 N., R. 9 E., as a scenic river.
“(210) Pratt river, washington.—The entirety of the Pratt River in the State of Washington, located in the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, to be administered by the Secretary of Agriculture as a wild river.” .

paragraph.heading: No condemnation.—
paragraph.content: No land or interest in land within the boundary of the river segment designated by paragraph (209) of section 3(a) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1274(a)) may be acquired by condemnation.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Nothing in paragraph (209) of section 3(a) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1274(a)) creates a protective perimeter or buffer zone outside the designated boundary of the river segment designated by that paragraph.

subparagraph.heading: Outside activities.—
subparagraph.content: The fact that an activity or use can be seen or heard within the boundary of the river segment designated by paragraph (209) of section 3(a) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1274(a)) shall not preclude the activity or use outside the boundary of the river segment.

section.heading: COLUMBINE-HONDO WILDERNESS.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Red river conveyance map.—
paragraph.content: The term “Red River Conveyance Map” means the map entitled “Town of Red River Town Site Act Proposal” and dated April 19, 2012.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of New Mexico.

paragraph.heading: Town.—
paragraph.content: The term “Town” means the town of Red River, New Mexico.

paragraph.heading: Village.—
paragraph.content: The term “Village” means the village of Taos Ski Valley, New Mexico.

paragraph.heading: Wilderness.—
paragraph.content: The term “Wilderness” means the Columbine-Hondo Wilderness designated by subsection (b)(1)(A).

paragraph.heading: Wilderness map.—
paragraph.content: The term “Wilderness Map” means the map entitled “Columbine-Hondo, Wheeler Peak Wilderness” and dated April 25, 2012.

subsection.heading: Addition to the National Wilderness Preservation System.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: In accordance with the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1131 et seq.), the approximately 45,000 acres of land in the Carson National Forest in the State, as generally depicted on the Wilderness Map, is designated as wilderness and as a component of the National Wilderness Preservation System, which shall be known as the “Columbine-Hondo Wilderness”.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Subject to valid existing rights, the Wilderness shall be administered by the Secretary in accordance with this section and the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1131 et seq.), except that any reference in that Act to the effective date of that Act shall be considered to be a reference to the date of enactment of this Act.

subclause.heading: In general.—
subclause.content: Congress does not intend for the designation of the Wilderness to create a protective perimeter or buffer zone around the Wilderness.

subclause.heading: Nonwilderness activities.—
subclause.content: The fact that nonwilderness activities or uses can be seen or heard from areas within the Wilderness shall not preclude the conduct of the activities or uses outside the boundary of the Wilderness.

subparagraph.heading: Incorporation of acquired land and interests in land.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Any land or interest in land that is within the boundary of the Wilderness that is acquired by the United States shall—

clause.content: become part of the Wilderness; and

clause.chapeau: be managed in accordance with—

subclause.content: the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1131 et seq.);
this subsection; and
any other applicable laws.

subparagraph.heading: Grazing.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Grazing of livestock in the Wilderness, where established before the date of enactment of this Act, shall be allowed to continue in accordance with—

clause.content: section 4(d)(4) of the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1133(d)(4)); and
the guidelines set forth in the report of the Committee on Interior and Insular Affairs of the House of Representatives accompanying H.R. 5487 of the 96th Congress (H. Rept. 96-617).

clause.heading: Finding.—
clause.content: Congress finds that, for purposes of section 103(a)(2) of Public Law 96-550 (16 U.S.C. 1132 note; 94 Stat. 3223), any Federal land in the Columbine-Hondo Wilderness Study Area administered by the Forest Service that is not designated as wilderness by subparagraph (A) has been adequately reviewed for wilderness designation.

clause.heading: Applicability.—
clause.content: The Federal land described in clause (i) is no longer subject to subsections (a)(2) and (b) of section 103 of Public Law 96-550 (16 U.S.C. 1132 note; 94 Stat. 3223).

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall prepare maps and legal descriptions of the Wilderness.

clause.heading: Force of law.—
clause.content: The maps and legal descriptions prepared under clause (i) shall have the same force and effect as if included in this section, except that the Secretary may correct errors in the maps and legal descriptions.

clause.heading: Public availability.—
clause.content: The maps and legal descriptions prepared under clause (i) shall be on file and available for public inspection in the appropriate offices of the Forest Service.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Nothing in this section affects the jurisdiction of the State with respect to fish and wildlife located on public land in the State, except that the Secretary may designate areas in which, and establish periods during which, for reasons of public safety, administration, or compliance with applicable laws, no hunting, fishing, or trapping will be permitted in the Wilderness.

clause.heading: Consultation.—
clause.content: Except in emergencies, the Secretary shall consult with the appropriate State agency and notify the public before taking any action under clause (i).

subparagraph.heading: Withdrawals.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Subject to valid existing rights, the Federal land described in subparagraphs (A) and (E)(i) and any land or interest in land that is acquired by the United States in the Wilderness after the date of enactment of this Act is withdrawn from—

clause.content: entry, appropriation, or disposal under the public land laws;
location, entry, and patent under the mining laws; and
operation of the mineral leasing, mineral materials, and geothermal leasing laws.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The boundary of the Wheeler Peak Wilderness in the State is modified as generally depicted in the Wilderness Map.

subparagraph.heading: Withdrawal.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Subject to valid existing rights, any Federal land added to or excluded from the boundary of the Wheeler Peak Wilderness under subparagraph (A) is withdrawn from—

clause.content: entry, appropriation, or disposal under the public land laws;
location, entry, and patent under the mining laws; and
operation of the mineral leasing, mineral materials, and geothermal leasing laws.

paragraph.heading: Town of red river land conveyance.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to the provisions of this paragraph, the Secretary shall convey to the Town, without consideration and by quitclaim deed, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to the one or more parcels of Federal land described in subparagraph (B) for which the Town submits a request to the Secretary by the date that is not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act.

subparagraph.heading: Description of land.—
subparagraph.content: The parcels of Federal land referred to in subparagraph (A) are the parcels of National Forest System land (including any improvements to the land) in Taos County, New Mexico, that are identified as “Parcel 1”, “Parcel 2”, “Parcel 3”, and “Parcel 4” on the Red River Conveyance Map.

subparagraph.heading: Conditions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The conveyance under subparagraph (A) shall be subject to—

clause.content: valid existing rights;
public rights-of-way through “Parcel 1”, “Parcel 3”, and “Parcel 4”;
an administrative right-of-way through “Parcel 2” reserved to the United States; and
such additional terms and conditions as the Secretary may require.

subparagraph.heading: Use of land.—
subparagraph.chapeau: As a condition of the conveyance under subparagraph (A), the Town shall use—

clause.content: “Parcel 1” for a wastewater treatment plant;
“Parcel 2” for a cemetery;
“Parcel 3” for a public park; and
“Parcel 4” for a public road.

subparagraph.heading: Reversion.—
subparagraph.content: In the quitclaim deed to the Town under subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall provide that any parcel of Federal land conveyed to the Town under subparagraph (A) shall revert to the Secretary, at the election of the Secretary, if the parcel of Federal land is used for a purpose other than the purpose for which the parcel was conveyed, as required under subparagraph (D).

clause.heading: Survey.—
clause.content: The exact acreage and legal description of the National Forest System land conveyed under subparagraph (A) shall be determined by a survey approved by the Secretary.

clause.heading: Costs.—
clause.content: The Town shall pay the reasonable survey and other administrative costs associated with the conveyance.

paragraph.heading: Village of taos ski valley land conveyance.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to the provisions of this paragraph, the Secretary shall convey to the Village, without consideration and by quitclaim deed, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to the parcel of Federal land described in subparagraph (B) for which the Village submits a request to the Secretary by the date that is not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act.

subparagraph.heading: Description of land.—
subparagraph.content: The parcel of Federal land referred to in subparagraph (A) is the parcel comprising approximately 4.6 acres of National Forest System land (including any improvements to the land) in Taos County generally depicted as “Parcel 1” on the map entitled “Village of Taos Ski Valley Town Site Act Proposal” and dated April 19, 2012.

subparagraph.heading: Conditions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The conveyance under subparagraph (A) shall be subject to—

clause.content: valid existing rights;
an administrative right-of-way through the parcel of Federal land described in subparagraph (B) reserved to the United States; and
such additional terms and conditions as the Secretary may require.

subparagraph.heading: Use of land.—
subparagraph.content: As a condition of the conveyance under subparagraph (A), the Village shall use the parcel of Federal land described in subparagraph (B) for a wastewater treatment plant.

subparagraph.heading: Reversion.—
subparagraph.content: In the quitclaim deed to the Village, the Secretary shall provide that the parcel of Federal land conveyed to the Village under subparagraph (A) shall revert to the Secretary, at the election of the Secretary, if the parcel of Federal land is used for a purpose other than the purpose for which the parcel was conveyed, as described in subparagraph (D).

clause.heading: Survey.—
clause.content: The exact acreage and legal description of the National Forest System land conveyed under subparagraph (A) shall be determined by a survey approved by the Secretary.

clause.heading: Costs.—
clause.content: The Village shall pay the reasonable survey and other administrative costs associated with the conveyance.

paragraph.heading: Authorization of sale of certain national forest system land.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Subject to the provisions of this paragraph and in exchange for consideration in an amount that is equal to the fair market value of the applicable parcel of National Forest System land, the Secretary may convey—

clause.content: to the holder of the permit numbered “QUE302101” for use of the parcel, the parcel of National Forest System land comprising approximately 0.2 acres that is generally depicted as “Parcel 5” on the Red River Conveyance Map; and

to the owner of the private property adjacent to the parcel, the parcel of National Forest System land comprising approximately 0.1 acres that is generally depicted as “Parcel 6” on the Red River Conveyance Map.

subparagraph.heading: Disposition of proceeds.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Any amounts received by the Secretary as consideration for a conveyance under subparagraph (A) shall be—

clause.content: deposited in the fund established under Public Law 90-171 (commonly known as the “Sisk Act”) (16 U.S.C. 484a); and
available to the Secretary, without further appropriation and until expended, for the acquisition of land or interests in land in Region 3 of the Forest Service.

subparagraph.heading: Conditions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The conveyance under subparagraph (A) shall be subject to—

clause.content: valid existing rights; and
such additional terms and conditions as the Secretary may require.

clause.heading: Survey.—
clause.content: The exact acreage and legal description of the National Forest System land conveyed under subparagraph (A) shall be determined by a survey approved by the Secretary.

clause.heading: Costs.—
clause.content: The reasonable survey and other administrative costs associated with the conveyance shall be paid by the holder of the permit or the owner of the private property, as applicable.

section.heading: HERMOSA CREEK WATERSHED PROTECTION.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: City.—
paragraph.content: The term “City” means the city of Durango, Colorado.

paragraph.heading: County.—
paragraph.content: The term “County” means La Plata County, Colorado.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: Special management area.—
paragraph.content: The term “Special Management Area” means the Hermosa Creek Special Management Area designated by subsection (b)(1).

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of Colorado.

subsection.heading: Designation of Hermosa Creek Special Management Area.—

paragraph.heading: Designation.—
paragraph.content: Subject to valid existing rights, certain Federal land in the San Juan National Forest comprising approximately 70,650 acres, as generally depicted on the map entitled “Proposed Hermosa Creek Special Management Area and Proposed Hermosa Creek Wilderness Area” and dated November 12, 2014, is designated as the “Hermosa Creek Special Management Area”.

paragraph.heading: Purpose.—
paragraph.content: The purpose of the Special Management Area is to conserve and protect for the benefit of present and future generations the watershed, geological, cultural, natural, scientific, recreational, wildlife, riparian, historical, educational, and scenic resources of the Special Management Area.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer the Special Management Area—

clause.content: in a manner that conserves, protects, and manages the resources of the Special Management Area described in paragraph (2); and

clause.chapeau: in accordance with—

subclause.content: the National Forest Management Act of 1976 (16 U.S.C. 1600 et seq.);
this Act; and
any other applicable laws.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Secretary shall allow only such uses of the Special Management Area as the Secretary determines would further the purposes described in paragraph (2).

subclause.heading: In general.—
subclause.content: Except as provided in subclause (II) and as needed for administrative purposes or to respond to an emergency, the use of motorized or mechanized vehicles in the Special Management Area shall be permitted only on roads and trails designated by the Secretary for use by those vehicles.

subclause.heading: Oversnow vehicles.—
subclause.chapeau: The Secretary shall authorize the use of snowmobiles and other oversnow vehicles within the Special Management Area—

item.content: when there exists adequate snow coverage; and
subject to such terms and conditions as the Secretary may require.

clause.heading: Grazing.—
clause.content: The Secretary shall permit grazing within the Special Management Area, if established before the date of enactment of this Act, subject to all applicable laws (including regulations) and Executive orders.

clause.heading: Prohibited activities.—
clause.chapeau: Within the area of the Special Management Area identified as “East Hermosa Area” on the map entitled “Proposed Hermosa Creek Special Management Area and Proposed Hermosa Creek Wilderness Area” and dated November 12, 2014, the following activities shall be prohibited:

subclause.content: New permanent or temporary road construction or the renovation of existing nonsystem roads, except as allowed under the final rule entitled “Special Areas; Roadless Area Conservation; Applicability to the National Forests in Colorado” (77 Fed. Reg. 39576 (July 3, 2012)).

Projects undertaken for the purpose of harvesting commercial timber (other than activities relating to the harvest of merchantable products that are byproducts of activities conducted for ecological restoration or to further the purposes described in this section).

paragraph.heading: State and federal water management.—
paragraph.chapeau: Nothing in this subsection affects the potential for development, operation, or maintenance of a water storage reservoir at the site in the Special Management Area that is identified in—

subparagraph.content: pages 17 through 20 of the Statewide Water Supply Initiative studies prepared by the Colorado Water Conservation Board and issued by the State in November 2004; and
page 27 of the Colorado Dam Site Inventory prepared by the Colorado Water Conservation Board and dated August 1996.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Subject to valid rights in existence on the date of enactment of this Act and except as provided in subparagraph (B), the Federal land within the Special Management Area is withdrawn from—

clause.content: all forms of entry, appropriation, and disposal under the public land laws;
location, entry, and patent under the mining laws; and
operation of the mineral leasing, mineral materials, and geothermal leasing laws.

subparagraph.heading: Exception.—
subparagraph.content: The withdrawal under subparagraph (A) shall not apply to the areas identified as parcels A and B on the map entitled “Proposed Hermosa Creek Special Management Area and Proposed Hermosa Creek Wilderness Area” and dated November 12, 2014.

paragraph.heading: Winter skiing and related winter activities.—
paragraph.chapeau: Nothing in this subsection alters or limits—

subparagraph.content: a permit held by a ski area;
the implementation of the activities governed by a ski area permit; or
the authority of the Secretary to modify or expand an existing ski area permit.

paragraph.heading: Vegetation management.—
paragraph.chapeau: Nothing in this subsection prevents the Secretary from conducting vegetation management projects within the Special Management Area—

subparagraph.chapeau: subject to—

clause.content: such reasonable regulations, policies, and practices as the Secretary determines to be appropriate; and
all applicable laws (including regulations); and

subparagraph.chapeau: in a manner consistent with—

clause.content: the purposes described in paragraph (2); and
this subsection.

paragraph.heading: Wildfire, insect, and disease management.—
paragraph.chapeau: In accordance with this subsection, the Secretary may—

subparagraph.content: carry out any measures that the Secretary determines to be necessary to manage wildland fire and treat hazardous fuels, insects, and diseases in the Special Management Area; and
coordinate those measures with the appropriate State or local agency, as the Secretary determines to be necessary.

paragraph.heading: Management plan.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall develop a management plan for the long-term protection and management of the Special Management Area that—

subparagraph.content: takes into account public input; and

provides for recreational opportunities to occur within the Special Management Area, including skiing, biking, hiking, fishing, hunting, horseback riding, snowmobiling, motorcycle riding, off-highway vehicle use, snowshoeing, and camping.

paragraph.heading: Trail and open area snowmobile usage.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this subsection affects the use or status of trails authorized for motorized or mechanized vehicle or open area snowmobile use on the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: State water rights.—
paragraph.chapeau: Nothing in this subsection affects access to, use of, or allocation of any absolute or conditional water right that is—

subparagraph.content: decreed under the laws of the State; and
in existence on the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Designation of wilderness.—
paragraph.content:
Section 2(a) of the Colorado Wilderness Act of 1993 (16 U.S.C. 1132 note; 107 Stat. 756; 114 Stat. 1955; 116 Stat. 1055) is amended by adding at the end the following:
“(22) Certain land within the San Juan National Forest that comprises approximately 37,236 acres, as generally depicted on the map entitled ‘Proposed Hermosa Creek Special Management Area and Proposed Hermosa Creek Wilderness Area’ and dated November 12, 2014, which shall be known as the ‘Hermosa Creek Wilderness’.” .

paragraph.heading: Effective date.—
paragraph.content: Any reference contained in the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1131 et seq.) to the effective date of that Act shall be considered to be a reference to the date of enactment of this Act for purposes of administering the wilderness area designated by section 2(a)(22) of the Colorado Wilderness Act of 1993 (16 U.S.C. 1132 note; 107 Stat. 756; 114 Stat. 1955; 116 Stat. 1055) (as added by paragraph (1)).

paragraph.heading: Fire, insects, and diseases.—
paragraph.content: In accordance with section 4(d)(1) of the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1133(d)(1)), within the wilderness areas designated by section 2(a)(22) of the Colorado Wilderness Act of 1993 (16 U.S.C. 1132 note; 107 Stat. 756; 114 Stat. 1955; 116 Stat. 1055) (as added by paragraph (1)), the Secretary may carry out any measure that the Secretary determines to be necessary to control fire, insects, and diseases, subject to such terms and conditions as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Withdrawal.—
paragraph.chapeau: Subject to valid existing rights, the land and mineral interests described in paragraph (2) are withdrawn from all forms of—

subparagraph.content: entry, appropriation, and disposal under the public land laws;
location, entry, and patent under the mining laws; and
disposition under all laws relating to mineral leasing, geothermal leasing, or mineral materials.

paragraph.heading: Description of land and mineral interests.—
paragraph.content: The land and mineral interests referred to in paragraph (1) are the Federal land and mineral interests generally depicted within the areas designated as “Withdrawal Areas” on the map entitled “Perins Peak & Animas City Mountain, Horse Gulch and Lake Nighthorse Mineral Withdrawal” and dated April 5, 2013.

paragraph.heading: Public purpose conveyance.—
paragraph.chapeau: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Secretary of the Interior may convey any portion of the land described in paragraph (2) that is administered by the Bureau of Land Management to the City, the County, or the State—

subparagraph.content: pursuant to the Act of June 14, 1926 (commonly known as the “Recreation and Public Purposes Act”) (43 U.S.C. 869 et seq.); or
by exchange in accordance with applicable laws (including regulations).

subsection.heading: Conveyance of Bureau of Land Management Land to County.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: On the expiration of the permit numbered COC 64651 (09) and dated February 24, 2009, on request and agreement of the County, the Secretary of the Interior shall convey to the County, without consideration and subject to valid existing rights, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to the land described in paragraph (2), subject to—

subparagraph.content: paragraph (3);
the condition that the County shall pay all administrative and other costs associated with the conveyance; and
such other terms and conditions as the Secretary of the Interior determines to be necessary.

paragraph.heading: Description of land.—
paragraph.content: The land referred to in paragraph (1) consists of approximately 82 acres of land managed by the Bureau of Land Management, Tres Rios District, Colorado, as generally depicted on the map entitled “La Plata County Grandview Conveyance” and dated May 5, 2014.

paragraph.heading: Use of conveyed land.—
paragraph.content: The Federal land conveyed pursuant to this subsection may be used by the County for any public purpose, in accordance with the Act of June 14, 1926 (commonly known as the “Recreation and Public Purposes Act”) (43 U.S.C. 869 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Reversion.—
paragraph.content: If the County ceases to use a parcel of the Federal land conveyed pursuant to this subsection in accordance with paragraph (1), title to the parcel shall revert to the Secretary of the Interior, at the option of the Secretary of the Interior.

subsection.heading: Molas Pass Recreation Area; Wilderness Study Area Release; Wilderness Study Area Transfer of Administrative Jurisdiction.—

subparagraph.heading: Designation.—
subparagraph.content: The approximately 461 acres of land in San Juan County, Colorado, that is generally depicted as “Molas Pass Recreation Area” on the map entitled “Molas Pass Recreation Area and Molas Pass Wilderness Study Area” and dated November 13, 2014, is designated as the “Molas Pass Recreation Area”.

subparagraph.heading: Use of snowmobiles.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The use of snowmobiles shall be authorized in the Molas Pass Recreation Area—

clause.content: during periods of adequate snow coverage;
in accordance with the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (43 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) and other applicable laws (including regulations);
on designated trails for winter motorized travel and grooming;
in designated areas for open area motorized travel; and
subject to such terms and conditions as the Secretary may require.

subparagraph.heading: Other recreational opportunities.—
subparagraph.content: In addition to the uses authorized under subparagraph (B), the Secretary may authorize other recreational uses in the Molas Pass Recreation Area.

subparagraph.heading: Transfer of administrative jurisdiction.—
subparagraph.content: Administrative jurisdiction over the Federal land generally depicted as “Molas Pass Wilderness Study Area” on the map entitled “Molas Pass Recreation Area and Molas Pass Wilderness Study Area”, and dated November 13, 2014, is transferred from the Bureau of Land Management to the Forest Service.

subparagraph.heading: Administration.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Federal land described in subparagraph (A) shall—
